entry.title: Length Is Cheap, Competition Is Not: Attention Predicts Context Rot in Retrieval
entry.summary: Length Is Cheap, Competition Is Not: Attention Predicts Context Rot in Retrieval arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines why language models fail at retrieval on long inputs. Across five open models, adding neutral filler barely reduces accuracy, while statements in the evidence format that give the queried key a rival value sharply lower it. The authors find that the attention left on the evidence best tracks the loss, and they release the probe and all 126K trial-level measurements. ★★★★ Notable: The authors attribute retrieval context rot to attention competition rather than length, reporting results across five open models and 126,473 trials, and releasing the probe and data.

entry.title: PACT: A training-free decoding rule that certifies the tokens actually written in diffusion language model generation
entry.summary: PACT: Certifying What Is Written in Parallel Decoding of Diffusion Language Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Parallel decoding lets masked diffusion language models write several tokens per forward pass, but existing commit rules test predicted distributions that do not reflect the tokens actually sampled. The paper proposes PACT, a training-free commit rule that samples tokens first, certifies the set to be written, and spaces positions within each step. Experiments on four LLaDA and Dream models across HumanEval, MBPP, GSM8K, MATH500 and IFEval show PACT matches published commit rules' quality with fewer forward passes.| ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose sampling tokens first and certifying the written set, proving no equal-guarantee rule commits more positions. entry.title: Evaluation Contracts and Evaluation Leverage: How Sliced Gaps Can Shift Without Model Changes
entry.summary: Evaluation Contracts and Evaluation Leverage: Sliced-Gap Readings in Structured Prediction Can Move Without Model Change arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper argues that sliced performance gaps, such as the intra-inter gap in document-level relation extraction, depend jointly on the model and the evaluation contract, including scoring function, gold version, threshold, and output format. With predictions held fixed, swapping the gold standard reverses a method ordering. The authors propose an evaluation leverage framework and EvalLever, a preregistered, audited evaluation workflow. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose an evaluation-leverage framework showing that frozen predictions can reverse method rankings under gold or scoring contract changes, plus an audited procedure and released workflow

entry.title: Structured priors: an algebra of component priors for prior-data fitted networks
entry.summary: Structured Priors: Towards an algebra of component priors for prior-data fitted networks arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Prior-data fitted networks are usually trained on synthetic data from one hand-built generator. This paper proposes structured priors, sets of named component priors linked by operators (mixture, convolution, amplitude scaling, local transform, projection) with proven algebraic properties, implemented in the macl2l package. A mixed prior of small components matched or beat every single component on seven of eight regression benchmarks. A pre-registered test of the model-averaging predictor failed, because the networks rarely identified the generating component. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose an algebra of structured priors with proven operator laws, evaluated on eight regression benchmarks, and report a failed pre-registered test.

entry.title: Physics-informed estimation of tensegrity prestress through cable slackening
entry.summary: Physics-Informed Identification of Tensegrity Prestress across Taut-Slack Transitions arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper formulates an inverse problem for identifying prestress, damping and axial stiffness in tensegrity structures from sparse measurements. Neural networks are trained on the equation-of-motion residual in constrained Cartesian coordinates, keeping a tension-only cable law so that slack cables are handled. The method is tested on simulated frames and on measured records of a biomimetic leg and a full-scale simplex, with reported identification errors. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend physics-informed networks from forward tensegrity response to inverse prestress identification across taut-slack transitions, reporting small errors on simulated and measured record

entry.title: Measure Before You Repair: An Explainable AI Agent for Blind 3-D MRI Artifact Correction
entry.summary: Measure Before You Repair: An Explainable Agent for Blind Restoration of Multi-Artifact 3-D MRI arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents Dx-Rx, an agent that uses a multimodal large language model to restore whole 3-D brain MRI volumes without knowing which artifacts are present. It first measures suspected artifacts such as noise, spikes, ghosting, bias field and motion with diagnostic tools, then applies repair tools and checks each result. It ends with a radiology-style report explaining its diagnoses and repairs. On 148 simulated T1-weighted volumes, the best model removed a mean 64.5% of artifact error, close to the 64.6% achieved when the true artifacts were supplied. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present a measure-then-repair MLLM agent restoring whole 3-D MRI volumes, reporting 64.5% artifact error removal across 148 simulated T1 volumes.

entry.title: Does an AI crowdfunding advisor favor founders by gender or ethnicity? An algorithm audit of LLM choices
entry.summary: Whose startup does the AI back? An algorithm audit of reputation and demographic signals in LLM-assisted crowdfunding arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines whether large language model assistants that advise backers on crowdfunding campaigns favor founders based on gender or ethnicity signals. In a pre-specified choice experiment, seven LLMs chose among five synthetic campaigns with randomized quality signals and founder names, yielding 40,248 responses. By default founder names had negligible effects, but when backers wanted to support underrepresented creators, models favored Black-signaled and female-signaled founders. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that LLM assistants favor Black and female founders only when backers seek to support underrepresented creators, across seven models and about 40,248 controlled choices.

entry.title: ProteoCraft: protein design framed as a propose-then-verify search
entry.summary: ProteoCraft: Protein Design as Proposal-Verification Search arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper treats protein design as a search optimization problem over combinatorial sequence space where structural evaluation is expensive. It introduces ProteoCraft, a tree-based search framework that uses approximate structural gradients from diffusion-based structure predictors to propose where to explore, and no-gradient folding model inference to verify sequences. Across fourteen de novo binder-design settings, the authors report improved design quality and high-confidence yield, and an 82.9% binding hit rate for PD-L1 miniproteins. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a tree-based search using diffusion-predictor gradients as proposal policies, evaluated across fourteen design settings and with prospective experiments.

entry.title: Forget What Comes Next: a statistical-independence method for unlearning in LLMs
entry.summary: Forget What Comes Next: LLM Unlearning via Statistical Independence arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces PINT, a machine unlearning algorithm for large language models that uses the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion (HSIC) to reduce statistical dependence between tokens to be forgotten and the internal representations used to predict them. The authors relate this objective to Exact Memorization through a computable upper bound. Experiments across eight settings, with models up to 70B parameters, cover unlearning Gaussian poisons, personal information, hazardous biology and cybersecurity knowledge, and copyrighted books and news. PINT achieves the best forgetting-utility trade-off on average and is the only method that makes Gaussian poisons undetectable while keeping utility near the original model. ★★★★ Notable: Uses HSIC to reduce dependence between forgotten tokens and predictive representations, with a computable bound to exact memorization; the authors report experiments across eight settings up to 70B.

entry.title: FlowBench: A training resource for counterfactual spatial imagination
entry.summary: FlowBench: Counterfactual Imagination Training for Spatial Intelligence arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper formalizes counterfactual spatial imagination, the ability to predict how a scene changes under hypothetical motions, and introduces FlowBench with 428K training examples across simulated and real-world scenes. Fine-tuning Qwen3-VL-8B on the simulated training split raises accuracy by 29.5 points in simulation and 16.9 points on real images. Training on FlowBench-Sim also raises Psi-0.6's text-to-flow prediction accuracy from 52.1% to 61.7%.

entry.title: Performance, Scalability and Maintenance: RPA vs. Autonomous Agents in Healthcare
entry.summary: Performance, Scalability and Maintenance: An Experimental Study of RPA vs. Autonomous Agents in the Healthcare Domain arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper compares two ways to retrieve mammography and breast ultrasound reports from a laboratory portal: a Playwright-based robotic process automation (RPA) solution and a large language model-based autonomous agent (APA). Across two rounds, RPA reached 98.90% accuracy versus 96.49% for APA and was far faster per patient. The authors conclude that RPA is superior when the interface is stable.

entry.title: AIRoA-0: Robot Manipulation Learned Entirely from Handheld Gripper Recordings
entry.summary: AIRoA-0: Long-Horizon, Precise, Cross-Embodiment Manipulation from Handheld Data arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents AIRoA-0 (A-0), a bimanual manipulation system trained on 16,151 hours of demonstrations recorded with the open-source handheld gripper YUBI, with no robot data collected at any stage. On ten evaluated tasks it reaches an average success rate of 78%, compared with 27% for the strongest of four other vision-language-action models post-trained on the same demonstrations. The system runs on several robot platforms that mount the YUBI gripper, and the dataset, pre-trained weights and post-training recipe are released. ★★★★ Notable: The authors train bimanual manipulation solely on handheld-gripper demonstrations, reporting 78% average success across ten tasks versus 27% for the best of four baselines.

entry.title: Unsatz: Testing whether AI can build scientific models from scratch
entry.summary: Unsatz: Evaluating Scientific Discovery Without a Given Ansatz arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces Unsatz, a benchmark where an LLM agent must decide the model structure itself, including which variables exist, which are hidden, and how they interact. The agent buys experiments within a budget and is scored on predicting unseen conditions, interventions, and longer runs. Across 80 systems in 20 domains, nine language models solved between 21% and 60% of tasks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a benchmark where agents build model structure themselves, reporting results across 80 systems and nine language models.

entry.title: ReconDreamer#: A self-evolving loop where reconstruction and generation improve each other for dynamic driving scenes
entry.summary: ReconDreamer#: Self-Evolving Closed-Loop Synergy of Reconstruction and Generation for Dynamic Driving Scenes arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents ReconDreamer#, a framework in which generative and reconstruction models iteratively refine each other to narrow the gap between synthesized novel-trajectory data and real sensor observations. It also adds a geometry-prior-based adaptive ground model to improve rendering quality. The method is evaluated on the Waymo, nuScenes, PandaSet, and EUVS benchmarks. On Waymo at a 6-m lateral shift, it improves NTA-IoU by 8.8% and NTL-IoU by 3.0%, and reduces FID by 15.1% relative to ReconDreamer++.

entry.title: Descending Everest, Part II: Oracle Complexity of Minimizing Convex (L0,L1)-Smooth Sums
entry.summary: Descending Everest, Part II: Oracle Complexity of Minimizing a Sum of Convex (L₀,L₁₎-Smooth Functions arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies minimizing the average of n convex (L0,L1)-smooth functions, where each function's Hessian norm is bounded by an affine function of its gradient norm. It derives upper and lower bounds on the number of oracle calls needed to reach expected function-value accuracy ε, which match up to logarithmic factors. The upper bound is achieved by the proposed YETI method, and the lower bound comes from explicit instance families that are hard for any first-order method.

entry.title: Rewriting Visible Context for Long Video Generation: The ReCR Training-Free Method
entry.summary: What Remains in Sight? Autoregressive Video Decoding as Representation-Guided Context Rewriting arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes ReCR, a training-free method that treats the choice of which past frames to show a decoder during autoregressive video generation as an explicit test-time decision. It uses internal decoder representations to select context units that match the global rollout state, avoid redundancy with recent content, cover temporal boundaries, and span diverse spatial layouts, then maps them onto a compact causal axis before decoding the next block. Across long-horizon text-to-video benchmarks, ReCR consistently improves several autoregressive backbones under matched visible-token budgets.

entry.title: A study of how features evolve in temporal difference learning
entry.summary: On the Feature Evolution of Temporal Difference Learning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how neural features emerge and spread during temporal-difference (TD) learning when network updates are incomplete, using finite-width two-layer ReLU critics on a constructed family of smooth stochastic MDPs. It shows that an informative TD update acquires the quadratic Bellman signal and achieves a strict finite-sample prediction-risk improvement over head-only SGD. The authors also derive a prediction-error transient bound and a regret bound for an exploration-then-commit algorithm.

entry.title: Nonparametric GARCH: A Neural Method for Volatility Estimation
entry.summary: Nonparametric GARCH: An Iterated Neural Estimator arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies nonparametric estimation and forecasting for GARCH-type volatility processes. It proposes an iterated neural estimator that alternates between estimating the recursion map and updating unobserved conditional variances. The authors establish finite-sample error bounds and show the estimator is minimax rate-optimal up to logarithmic factors. Simulations and real-data applications indicate the method performs competitively under nonlinear and time-varying volatility.

entry.title: Improving Prostate MRI Scoring and Cancer Detection Using Anatomical Zone Guidance
entry.summary: Improving PI-RADS Prediction and Prostate Cancer Detection from Multiparametric MRI with Anatomical Guidance arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper tests whether adding prostate zonal masks to multiparametric MRI improves prediction of PI-RADS scores and detection of clinically significant prostate cancer. The authors evaluate several architectures, including 3D ResNet-18, ResNet-50, and ViT, on a large internal dataset. Anatomical guidance generally improved performance, and fine-tuned results on external datasets supported these benefits.

entry.title: Palimpsestic Accountability in US Federal AI Inventories: How Repeated Releases Rewrite Oversight Records
entry.summary: Palimpsestic Accountability in the US Federal AI Inventories arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper compares three releases of the US Federal AI Use Case Inventory from 2023 to 2025, linking entries across versions and analyzing only questions that both releases required. The inventory grew from 710 to 3,611 entries and fewer required answers were left blank, but accountability was rewritten through changed question scopes, agency-assigned classifications that gated reporting, and overwritten answers, with little account of human oversight. The authors term this condition palimpsestic accountability and recommend versioned records, reasons for every reclassification, and documented oversight.

entry.title: AdSteer: Native Advertising Within Large Language Model Responses
entry.summary: AdSteer: Native Advertising in Large Language Model Generation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes AdSteer, a lightweight framework that integrates advertisements into large language model responses during decoding by adaptively adjusting token probabilities. It calibrates the strength and duration of the advertising influence so that sponsored content fits naturally into the response. Experiments on GEM-Bench across three application scenarios report a 14.1% average gain in overall score over the strongest baselines and 22.5% fewer total tokens than rewrite-based methods.

entry.title: RGDM: a diffusion model that generates clean synthetic graph structures even when trained on adversarially attacked graphs.
entry.summary: RGDM: Robust Graph Diffusion Model arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces the Robust Graph Diffusion Model (RGDM), which generates labeled synthetic graph structures of nodes and edges that can be merged into a given graph. RGDM combines a Robust Graph Autoencoder (RGAE) with a Latent Diffusion Model (LDM), using an edge selection mechanism and low-rank regularization on latent features. Experiments show that graph neural networks trained on the augmented graph exhibit improved robustness against various graph adversarial attacks in semi-supervised node classification.

entry.title: Early stopping for web agents using interpretable failure patterns
entry.summary: Interpretable Early Termination of Web Navigation Agents via Closed Sequential Pattern Mining arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper applies closed sequential pattern mining (BIDE+) to the first K steps of web navigation agent traces, producing a small, reviewable library of failure signatures grouped into a four-category failure taxonomy with repair recommendations. The method is evaluated on 1,544 MiniWoB++ traces from three open-weight language models, with contamination artifacts removed. At K=3 it reaches an F1 of 0.717 in the Exclude-errors configuration, and an early-termination policy saves 26.3% of tokens at 92% precision.

entry.title: Where Do Distilled Students Store Thinking?
entry.summary: Where Do Distilled Students Store Thinking? arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Small student models lose accuracy on the long solutions of large reasoning models, so some work shortens these solutions by interpolating a reasoning model with a short-answer model at ratio λ. The authors compare LoRA adapters of three students from three teacher pairs at each λ and find that the adapters' update subspace changes most where the teacher stops thinking and solutions shorten most. They identify a shared adapter subspace tied to thinking-like behavior, and removing it largely turns that behavior off across pairs, students and benchmarks.

entry.title: COSMIO: A benchmark for predicting how astronomical objects look in other sky surveys
entry.summary: COSMIO: A Benchmark for Cross-Survey Modality Imputation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Large astronomical surveys each observe only some objects, with different resolutions, wavelengths, and noise. This paper formalizes cross-survey modality imputation, the task of inferring an object's appearance in surveys where it was not observed, and introduces COSMIO, an aligned benchmark built from LSST, Euclid, and Roman observations. Existing imputation methods transfer poorly to this setting. Performance also degrades for rare events such as strong gravitational lenses, and this degradation carries over to downstream lens detection.

entry.title: LoopKV: Loop-Aware KV Cache Compression for Looped Transformers
entry.summary: LoopKV: Loop-Aware KV Cache Compression for Serving Looped Transformers arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Looped transformers reuse a shared block several times per token to gain accuracy without extra parameters, but keeping a separate KV cache for each loop uses a lot of memory. LoopKV runs a one-time offline profile to assign each (loop, layer) cell 4-bit storage, 2-bit storage, or reuse of the final loop's KV, minimizing reads under damage and storage budgets. On Ouro-1.4B, its memory-optimized plan stores 35% less KV than uniform 4-bit quantization (KIVI-4) and reaches 1.7-2.2x KIVI-4's goodput under a latency objective.

entry.title: GlucoAgent: a system that forecasts blood sugar using personal data from multiple sources
entry.summary: GlucoAgent: Personalized Glucose Forecasting from Multimodal Personal Context arXiv · Nov 3, 2026GlucoAgent is an AI agent built on a large language model that predicts glucose levels using multimodal personal data such as continuous glucose monitor readings, smartwatch data, meal logs, and health profiles. For each forecast, it writes and runs code to analyze this data and returns a prediction with its reasoning and supporting evidence. On the CGMacros dataset, it achieves an average RMSE of 22.5 mg/dL, outperforming the Chronos-2 foundation model at 23.5 mg/dL, and gains more from multimodal data, especially in post-meal windows.

entry.title: An automated photometric pipeline for measuring spiral galaxy corotation radii
entry.summary: An automated photometric pipeline for measuring the corotation radius of spiral galaxies arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents an automated photometric pipeline that identifies the corotation radius of spiral galaxies by tracking the azimuthal phase offset between young and old stellar populations. Benchmarked against published measurements on 90 galaxies with reference values, it places a correct corotation radius in 80.0% of cases and achieves a recall-purity harmonic mean of 0.58, the highest among the compared methods. The pipeline is run on the full reference sample without pre-selection.

entry.title: Evolution Strategies Paradox: Better Models from Worse Perturbations
entry.summary: The Evolution Strategies Paradox: Better Models from Worse Perturbations arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how Evolution Strategies (ES), a perturbation-based method, can fine-tune billion-parameter large language models. It identifies a paradox in which every perturbed offspring model performs worse than the parent, yet the parent consistently improves during training. The authors explain this through the local reward landscape and properties of the ES estimator: exploration in high-dimensional spaces lowers performance but still points toward good directions, and aggregating these directions enables local improvement.

entry.title: Co-occurrence Biases Overriding Visual Evidence in Vision-Language Models for Construction Hazard Alarms
entry.summary: Co-Occurrence Priors Override Visual Spatial Evidence: Understanding False Alarms in Vision-Language Models for Construction Struck-By Hazard Detection arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This study examines why vision-language models give false struck-by hazard warnings on construction sites. The authors tested Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3.5-8B on 355 counterfactual worker-excavator scene pairs, using behavioral analysis, representation probing, and interventions. Both models recognized entities and encoded spatial relations, yet many distant scenes were still flagged as hazardous, indicating that false alarms mainly arise from decision-making rather than recognition or spatial encoding.

entry.title: Generalizable AI-generated image detection with explanations grounded in embedding space (the FOX method)
entry.summary: Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection with Embedding-Space Explanations arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents FOX, a method for detecting AI-generated images that also provides explanations. It first builds and freezes a specialist DINOv3-based detector, then uses its visual representation to guide a lightweight vision-language model toward forensic explanations, so explanation training does not change the verdict. The authors report a mean AUC of 97.4 across 14 unseen generators, a BERTScore of 69.8 on XPlainVerse, and 56.1 on LOKI.

entry.title: Separating shared and task-specific directions for data-free model merging (CUSD)
entry.summary: Separating Common and Unique Directions for Data-Free Model Merging arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes CUSD (Common--Unique Subspace Decomposition), a data-free method for merging fine-tuned models. It splits each task vector into common and unique directional components, merges the common parts with an arithmetic operator, and keeps the unique residuals separately. Experiments on 11 base models, four model families, and four arithmetic merging operators report improvements in 42 of 44 combinations, with gains of up to 22.5%. The code is publicly available.

entry.title: Say Less, Mean Better: Training-Free Control of Language Model Verbosity
entry.summary: Say Less, Mean Better: Training-Free Verbosity Control for Language Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces MinimalLM, a training-free framework that controls how long large language models respond. It combines uncertainty-aware, length-dependent stop-token adjustment with structural completeness checks to decide when generation should end. Across three open-source models and 330 questions, it cut generated tokens by 47.6% and sped up individual responses by 19-68%. Its quality score was 8.04/10, close to the 8.42/10 of unmodified models.

entry.title: Why pretraining data transfers: structure, dimensionality, and distribution shape, and why the input pipeline decides which matters
entry.summary: Structure, Dimensionality, and Distribution Shape - What Makes Pretraining Data Transferable, and Why the Input Pipeline Decides Which arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines what makes a pretraining corpus transferable, describing it by its structure, dimensionality, and the distribution shape of each unit's values. The authors propose the Transfer-Invariance Principle, arguing that the model's input transform, rather than the data modality, determines which properties matter for transfer. To test this, they build TransferForge, a generator of synthetic populations with prescribed properties, and run experiments under two model input settings.

entry.title: ModelBlaster: Learning-Augmented AI Agents That Speed Up Code Across Models, Kernels, and Hardware
entry.summary: ModelBlaster: Closing the Performance Gap through Learning-Augmented Agents Across Models, Kernels and Hardware Backends arXiv · Nov 3, 2026ModelBlaster is a framework that uses memory-augmented in-context reinforcement learning to optimize data-parallel kernels and whole models across different SIMD and SIMT accelerators. Its policy is a persistent knowledge base updated at inference time, letting experience carry across kernels, models, and hardware targets. The paper reports geometric-mean speedups over PyTorch on KernelBench and SOL-ExecBench on a B200 GPU, plus gains over vendor SDKs and other compilers on Qualcomm and RISC-V hardware.

entry.title: Can This 3D Asset Be Reused? A Diagnostic Method Beyond Beauty Renders
entry.summary: Is This 3D Asset Usable? Beyond the Beauty Render for Asset Curation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces Diagnostic Rendered Evidence (DRE), which judges whether a 3D asset can be reliably reused by scoring beauty, wireframe, and UV-seam renders with frozen ViT classifiers and combining the results. On 1,234 human-labeled TexVerse assets it reaches 86.36% balanced accuracy and 88.32% bad-asset recall. On a separate balanced 764-asset external test it reaches 88.9% balanced reference-label accuracy. At inference it needs only the imported asset and renderer-derived evidence.

entry.title: Structured clinical memory as context for probabilistic decision models, tested on synthetic cases with Jev
entry.summary: Structured Clinical Memory as Context for Probabilistic Decision Models: A Synthetic Evaluation with Jev arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper asks whether a compact structured memory of a patient's history improves a probabilistic decision model's answers when the patient vignette is already provided. The authors built 30 fully synthetic cases across twelve clinical domains, paired each with synthetic structured memory, and evaluated 120 questions using Jev. Adding memory raised accuracy from 90.0% to 93.3% and lowered log loss and Brier scores, though the accuracy difference was not statistically significant.

entry.title: Agent Board: a durable kanban-style coordination layer for agents that outlive a single conversation
entry.summary: The Agent Board: Kanban for Machines; Durable Coordination for Agents That Outlive the Conversation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents the Agent Board, a coordination substrate in the Corvic harness: a durable shared table where agents post, watch, and block on semi-structured tasks without holding a process while they wait. A system agent, the Board Keeper, carries events from outside the agent system onto the board, matches them to waiting tasks by reading their text, and allocates agents for tasks that name a kind of agent. In three small simulated pilots, the board's wait cost stayed flat as wait length grew while naive polling grew about 165-fold, but a plain external watcher was cheaper; the Board Keeper produced no false wakes but missed 3.6 percent of real wakes.

entry.title: ScaleTraj: Generating Human Movement Paths by Splitting Trips Across Spatial Scales
entry.summary: ScaleTraj: Scale-Decomposed Human Trajectory Generation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses generating realistic individual human movement trajectories while also matching population-level mobility patterns. The authors formalize the Population-Level Displacement Gap, where bottom-up generated populations fail to reproduce the heavy-tailed displacement distribution, and introduce the Scale Fidelity Profile to diagnose it. They propose ScaleTraj, an autoregressive Transformer that first selects a movement scale and then predicts the destination conditioned on that scale. Experiments on two datasets show that ScaleTraj reduces this gap compared with model-driven and data-driven baselines while preserving fidelity.

entry.title: CHROMA-MILL: Joint Low-Light Enhancement and White Balance Under Colored Light
entry.summary: CHROMA-MILL: Joint Low-Light Enhancement and White Balance under Colored Illumination arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces CHROMA-MILL, a RAW image dataset of 50 scenes captured with a DSLR and a smartphone under four calibrated illuminants at eleven intensity levels. Captures are blended in the linear RAW domain to create physically valid illuminant mixtures with exact chromaticity ground truth. The authors propose CTI-Retinexformer, which jointly supervises an illumination map, a chromaticity prediction, and an illumination-invariant scene embedding. It outperforms the best cascaded approach by 0.7 dB PSNR_L and 1.1 ΔE00.

entry.title: Same rule, different verdicts: how rubric language and wording affect LLM judges in Korean support dialogues
entry.summary: Same Rule, Different Verdicts: Rubric Language and Clause Structure in LLM Judges for Korean Support Dialogues arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines whether an LLM judge's verdict depends on the language of its evaluation rubric and on how each rubric item is worded. The authors wrote 12 criteria in four clause structures (affirmative, negated, conditional, exception), provided each in Korean and English, and had seven models judge translated ESConv dialogues and boundary cases. Cross-provider agreement was lower with Korean rubrics than with English ones, and disagreement concentrated in negated, conditional, and exception items.

entry.title: Changing the LLM judge changes system rankings: a preregistered study of cross-provider replication
entry.summary: Swapping the Judge Changes the Ranking: A Preregistered Study of Cross-Provider Replication in LLM-Judged System Comparisons arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This preregistered study re-judges 4,000 human-voted Chatbot Arena battles with five LLM judges from three providers to test whether conclusions can be replicated with a judge from another provider. Agreement with human votes is low, and system rankings shift substantially depending on the judge used. The preregistered hypothesis that rankings remain stable was not supported.

entry.title: ScienceVision: Can AI Observe and Reason Like a Scientist?
entry.summary: ScienceVision: Can AI Observe and Reason Like a Scientist? arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces ScienceVision, a benchmark testing whether AI models can understand and reason about scientific 3D data across biology, chemistry, medical imaging, mechanical CAD, and architecture. It contains 250 expert-level visual question answering items, 50 per domain, built with synthetic generation and expert review. Across 12 models, the best mean score was 0.53 out of 1. Workflows using native 3D artifacts outperformed rendered 2D images for every model, by 17.2 percentage points on average.

entry.title: Follow the Features: Using sparse autoencoder features to select small instruction-tuning datasets for language models
entry.summary: Follow the Features: SAE Feature-Guided Data-Efficient Instruction-Tuning of Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces Follow the Features (FtF), a method that uses sparse autoencoder (SAE) features to pick a small subset of instruction-tuning data. It ranks features by dataset-level activation statistics, scores samples by how strongly they express top-ranked features, and resamples features to promote diversity. At a 100-sample budget, FtF performs competitively with GRAPE and S2L, and on Qwen 3 8B trained on Alpaca it beats full-dataset training on the harmonic mean of AlpacaEval win rate and Open LLM Leaderboard score, though full-dataset training scores higher on the Leaderboard alone.

entry.title: From Visual Matching to Textual Conditioning: Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation via Reference Inversion
entry.summary: From Visual Matching to Textual Conditioning: Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation via Reference Inversion arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses cross-domain few-shot segmentation, which segments objects in unseen domains using only a few annotated references. The authors propose RI-SAM3, which builds on SAM3's text-conditioned segmentation by learning suitable textual tokens for each target category instead of relying on visual matching. With SAM3 frozen, the method optimizes about 12K parameters per category and reports superior performance across multiple benchmarks.

entry.title: RAPID: Faster Internal Distillation Using Randomized Projections
entry.summary: RAPID: Increasing Efficiency of Internal Distillation via Randomized Methods arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces RAPID, a method for distilling a teacher model's internal representations into a smaller student model. Existing approaches learn projection matrices to match dimensions, and these are discarded after training, which wastes compute. RAPID replaces learned projections with randomized projections based on the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma, and combines exponential moving average with homoscedastic uncertainty weighting in its objective. In post-training experiments on reasoning tasks, RAPID improves training efficiency by up to 21.1% while performing comparably to existing methods.

entry.title: AlgoPilot: Cross-Paradigm Reasoning in Language Models via Strategy Selection
entry.summary: AlgoPilot: Cross-Paradigm Reasoning in Language Models via Strategy Selection and Guidance arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes AlgoPilot, a framework that helps language models first choose a suitable problem-solving paradigm, then formulate the problem in structured form before execution. It has three parts: SteerLM selects the strategy, GuideLM generates formulation guidance for that strategy, and ExecutionLM produces the solution. Built on Qwen3-8B and tested on 13 benchmarks across 5 problem categories, it raises average accuracy from 38.4% to 72.9%. The authors also report that the learned steering and formulation modules transfer across execution models.

entry.title: How hard it is to build a ReLU network from a fixed set of parameter values
entry.summary: The Complexity of ReLU Network Synthesis from a Parameter Multiset arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies whether a ReLU neural network with a bounded number of neurons can be built so that, with its weights and biases taken from a given multiset of rational numbers, it meets a target behavior. It analyzes the computational complexity of this synthesis problem under different requirements, such as exact agreement on examples, agreement on all inputs, or a bound on expected loss. The results range from NP-complete to Σ2P-, DP- and NP^PP-complete, depending on the setting.

entry.title: Tutorial-Conditioned Computer-Use Agents Gain Little from World Models
entry.summary: Computer-Use Agents Gain Little Benefit from a World Model When Conditioned on Tutorials arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper isolates the contributions of tutorials, a judge, and world models to computer-use agents. The authors build two tutorial datasets, OSWorld-Tutorial and ScienceBoard-Tutorial, and propose RAG-PolicyJudge, where a policy proposes actions and a judge selects among them. They find that with tutorials present, even perfect visual future observations give little benefit, and error analysis points to the judge's reasoning over future states and task completion as the bottleneck.

entry.title: Finite-sample convergence of multi-agent learning on networks, and how entropy regularization helps
entry.summary: Finite-Sample Convergence in Networked Average Reward MARL: Decentralization Pitfalls and Entropy Remedies arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies average reward multi-agent reinforcement learning, where agents in a network each update using only information from their k-hop neighborhood while jointly maximizing total network reward. It first proves impossibility results for converging to globally optimal joint policies in this decentralized setting. It then gives finite-sample guarantees for a decentralized actor-critic algorithm with linear function approximation, converging to an approximate stationary point with small gradient norm. Adding fixed-state entropy regularization is shown to reshape the objective landscape and yield stronger global convergence guarantees for this algorithm.

entry.title: Conformal prediction that stays accurate for each part of a graph, not just on average
entry.summary: Graph-Localized Coverage for Conformal Prediction on Inductive Graphs arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces GLocalCP, an online conformal prediction framework for inductive node classification and edge prediction on graphs. It combines marginal and graph-local calibration, using a nonconformity score based on mutual information from Monte-Carlo dropout. Experiments show that similar overall coverage can hide very different local reliability, and that GLocalCP reduces local calibration error while shrinking prediction sets.

entry.title: TB-Transolver: Faster, Coherent Long-Range Forecasts for Time-Dependent Physics Simulations via Temporal Bundling
entry.summary: TB-Transolver: Parallelized and Coherent Long-Horizon Rollouts via Temporal Bundling for Time-Dependent PDEs arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents TB-Transolver, which scales the Transolver model to time-dependent PDEs by grouping snapshots into temporal bundles. It also introduces a spatiotemporal coherence metric that uses only training data to choose bundle widths in advance. Across plasticity, fluid dynamics, reaction-diffusion, and global weather forecasting, the method trains up to 29 times faster than autoregressive and time-conditioned baselines. Multi-node, multi-GPU parallelism further raises the aggregated speedup to as much as 45.6 times for highly coherent systems.

entry.title: StreamLTT: Risk Certification for Choosing Policies in Dependent Data Streams
entry.summary: StreamLTT: Risk Certification for Policy Selection under Stream Dependence arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces StreamLTT, a method for certifying deployment policies against a prescribed risk target when losses are dependent and change over time. It replaces the fixed population risk with an average predictable risk, conditioning each decision's loss on information available before its outcome is revealed. Combined with family-wise error rate control, it yields a simultaneously certified policy region. Across seven forecasting datasets and seven deployment risks, its certified frontier lies closer to the risk target than several alternative methods, while empirical family-wise error closely follows the prescribed level.

entry.title: On the Primacy Bias in RLVR Training
entry.summary: On the Primacy Bias in RLVR Training arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines whether Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Reward (RLVR) can extend the reasoning abilities of large language models beyond what the base model already encodes. Through the lens of primacy bias, the authors show that RLVR on mixed data mainly sharpens performance on easier problems, with only marginal gains on harder ones. Hard problems contribute most to expanding reasoning, but prolonged training on them may cause forgetting on easy problems.

entry.title: Query-based submodular data selection for efficient instruction tuning
entry.summary: Query-based Submodular Data Selection for Efficient Instruction Tuning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes QSGS, a method for choosing a small subset of training examples from a large, mixed pool to fine-tune language models on a target task. It frames selection as a submodular graph cut over a gradient similarity graph, balancing relevance to the target with a penalty on redundancy among selected examples. A gradient-guided step synthesizes examples for under-covered target directions. Experiments on MMLU, BBH, and TydiQA with Llama-2, Llama-3, and Mistral report larger gains as the data budget shrinks.

entry.title: Predicting Before Launch: Learned Throughput Forecasting for Choosing Hardware in a Production Training Fleet
entry.summary: Look Before You Launch: Learned Throughput Prediction for Hardware Selection in a Production Training Fleet arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents LEAP, a machine learning service that predicts each training job's throughput on every candidate hardware type at submission time and ranks the options by predicted throughput per unit cost. It routes tens of thousands of job attempts daily across hundreds of model types and more than 20 hardware types in a production fleet. Over 30 nightly retrains, LEAP reports 77% accuracy, and the share of eligible training GPU-hours receiving a ranking rose from 58% to 95% over six months. The authors estimate savings of about 3% in training computational cost.

entry.title: HybridSpec: Throughput-aware speculative decoding for hybrid GDN-MoE language models
entry.summary: HybridSpec: Throughput-Aware Speculative Decoding for Hybrid GDN-MoE Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies speculative decoding for hybrid language models that combine Gated DeltaNet and mixture-of-experts layers, where verification cost grows quickly with the number of draft tokens checked. The authors propose HybridSpec, which chooses the verification length on the GPU using acceptance estimates and measured latency, applies a lightweight routing check to keep or drop a token, and uses block-parallel kernels to reconstruct recurrent states. In single-request greedy decoding on three such models, HybridSpec is reported to be 1.75 to 1.88 times faster than autoregressive decoding and 1.30 to 1.33 times faster than DFlash.

entry.title: Forgetting to Improve: a principled way to remove harmful data in active learning
entry.summary: Forgetting to Improve: Principled Data Removal in Active Learning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes Forgetting to Improve, a method for cases where model mismatch means some data harms modeling for a specific task. The authors derive an influence function for Gaussian process models that allows detrimental data samples to be removed in a principled way. The approach is reported to give significant improvements on Bayesian optimization, model-based reinforcement learning, and transductive learning.

entry.title: Deep learning to sharpen and denoise 4D heart blood-flow MRI scans
entry.summary: Spatial and Temporal Super-Resolution and Denoising of Intracardiac 4D Flow MRI arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces 4D-MRAR, a deep learning method that improves 4D Flow MRI of blood flow inside the heart by increasing spatial and temporal resolution and reducing noise. It combines a residual convolutional network, a recurrent network, and an implicit neural field, and enforces fluid flow governing equations during training. The model was trained on left ventricle simulation data and tested on synthetic whole-heart data and real scans.

entry.title: Exploit or conform? How prompting for norm utility changes LLMs' use of community beliefs
entry.summary: Exploit or conform? How norm utility prompting changes the way LLMs use community beliefs arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies how three open-weight large language models make one-shot decisions in two-player social dilemmas when told what the community believes. Without guidance on how those beliefs should matter, cooperation in the Snowdrift game fell as community belief in cooperation rose. When the components of norm utility were explicitly prompted, this relationship reversed and cooperation increased, broadly matching a simple norm utility model. Norm utility prompting also reduced the volatility of decisions across changing social contexts and produced more consistent reasoning across models.

entry.title: Denoising as Stein: learning hidden structure in diffusion models via moments
entry.summary: Denoising Is Stein: Moment Access and a Resource Hierarchy for Learning Hidden Structure in Diffusion Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies learning a score function from denoising pairs when data contains a hidden non-Gaussian component. If covariance reveals the component, its subspace is recovered directly; if covariance is isotropic, the learner must extract the first distinguishing moment. It gives exponent results for feature and sample requirements across learners and proposes a two-stage method that obtains a fixed score gain over the Gaussian baseline.

entry.title: Testing whether logits processors get the right inputs in speculative decoding engines
entry.summary: Testing Processor Contracts in Speculative Decoding Engines arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Speculative sampling speeds up text decoding without changing the target output distribution, but this guarantee assumes that constraint-enforcing processors receive the correct token prefix and state at each step. The paper formalizes this requirement as a processor-prefix contract and introduces BADC, a branch-aware differential conformance testing method. Experiments on selected Transformers and llama-cpp-python releases confirm two causes of failure: processors reading unverified drafts, or advancing state without rollback.

entry.title: When Model Complexity Helps in Predicting Brain Responses to Movies Across People
entry.summary: When Model Complexity Matters in Cross-Subject Naturalistic fMRI Prediction arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines when more complex neural models are useful for predicting blood-oxygen-level-dependent (BOLD) brain responses to naturalistic stimuli. The authors compare linear and nonlinear predictors on three public fMRI datasets, with and without recently measured BOLD history. They report that pretrained visual features generally outperform raw pixels, and that measured history gives substantial gains that generally shrink as rollouts lengthen.

entry.title: Recursa: A Self-Improving Foundation Model System
entry.summary: Recursa: Toward Recursively Self-Improving Foundation Model Systems arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces Recursa, a foundation model system that adapts to new domains by learning from its own experience, without human experts or a stronger teacher model. It stores domain skills, guidance on when to apply them, past task experiences, and reflections in a knowledge repository, which it refines through recursive self-improvement using parallel learners. On Harvey LAB's Firm Knowledge benchmark, the all-pass rate on held-out tasks rose from 30.0% to 55.0% with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and from 35.0% to 46.0% with Qwen3.8-Flash.

entry.title: Do Pretrained Backbones Transfer to Physical Sensors? Multimodal Initialization Study
entry.summary: Do Pretrained Backbones Transfer to Physical Sensors? A Systematic Study of Multimodal Initialization Across the Sensor Stack arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines how well pretrained vision backbones transfer to multi-sensor autonomous driving tasks. The authors assemble 2.82M images from 16 public datasets, covering physical sensor modalities such as RGB, LWIR, NIR, and event cameras, plus model-derived modalities like stereo depth and segmentation. They perform in-domain MultiMAE-based pretraining and compare it against ViT, MAE, DINO, and MultiMAE backbones on downstream sensor fusion tasks. They report that MultiMAE is a strong out-of-the-box baseline that transfers even to unseen modalities, and their targeted modifications give modest but consistent gains.

entry.title: ROCm InferaSim: a tool that predicts LLM serving performance to cut configuration trial costs
entry.summary: ROCm InferaSim: Cut LLM Serving Trial Costs and Deploy the Best Configuration arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents ROCm InferaSim, which predicts large language model serving performance from a few short measurements instead of exhaustively testing every configuration. It benchmarks each distinct kernel set once on at most one node and extends those results to other deployments with analytical laws. On AMD MI355X GPUs, 11 anchors took 9.1 GPU-hours, versus 204 GPU-hours to measure the 226 configurations they cover. Time per output token has 8.1% median error across 172 configurations, and throughput is within 5.5% for 159 disaggregated deployments not used as anchors.

entry.title: Language Model Augmented Decision Transformer for Multi-Task Offline RL
entry.summary: Language Model Augmented Decision Transformer for Multi-Task Offline Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses two problems in offline multi-task reinforcement learning: scarce data per task and limited generalization across tasks. It proposes LaMA-DT, which uses one large language model to generate task-aligned trajectories from natural-language task descriptions, filter them for quality, and then serve as a language-conditioned Decision Transformer fine-tuned on real and augmented data. Experiments on Meta-World and MuJoCo benchmarks show it consistently outperforms competitive baselines, especially in low-data settings.

entry.title: Compression Forcing: Hierarchical History Tokenization for Flexible World Models
entry.summary: Compression Forcing: Hierarchical History Tokenization Enables Flexible World Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes Compression Forcing, a framework that aligns history compression with the predictive goals of world modeling. Its Dynamics-Aware Tokenization compresses past observations into a sequence ordered by decreasing dynamics saliency, enabling Hierarchical History Guidance on a diffusion backbone during inference. Experiments across environments report improved prediction fidelity, physical realism, and downstream decision-making.

entry.title: A practical causal framework for mobile robots moving from simulation to real human spaces
entry.summary: A Practical Causal Framework for Autonomous Mobile Robots: From Simulation to Real-World Human Environments arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents a causal inference framework that helps mobile robots reason about why events happen, enabling safer and more efficient decisions. It transfers causal relations learned in simulation to the real world by keeping the high-level causal structure fixed and updating only the causal model parameters with a limited set of new observations. The framework runs onboard a mobile robot and, according to the authors, significantly outperforms a non-causal baseline in navigating safely in complex human-shared scenarios.

entry.title: DUNEDepth: Estimating Bronchoscope Depth and Camera Pose by Adapting a 3D-Vision Foundation Model
entry.summary: DUNEDepth: Bronchoscopic Depth and Pose Estimation via Hybrid Adaptation of a 3D-Vision Foundation Model arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents DUNEDepth, a model that estimates depth and camera motion from bronchoscopy exam videos so they can be linked to a patient's pre-operative 3D chest CT scan. It combines a shared DUNE ViT encoder, a twin MASt3R cross-attention decoder, and a prediction head drawing on MASt3R and Reloc3r. Training uses a hybrid strategy of synthetic supervised and self-supervised learning, drawing on bronchoscopic video and CT-derived virtual bronchoscopic views. Experiments show more accurate depth and camera trajectory estimates than previously proposed self-supervised methods.

entry.title: SurgEye: A Surgical Scene Reasoning Framework That Needs No Instruction Tuning
entry.summary: SurgEye: Instruction Tuning-Free Perception-Reasoning Framework for Surgical Scene Understanding arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents SurgEye, a framework for understanding surgical scenes that avoids instruction tuning on large question-answer datasets. It uses a vision foundation model with routed multi-task perception to extract spatial and temporal evidence, and a frozen large language model that coordinates these perception tools to compose grounded answers. The authors also build SurgEye-Bench, covering eight surgical procedures with perception labels for verifiable evaluation, and report that SurgEye outperforms state-of-the-art methods in surgical reasoning.

entry.title: Task-aware Decision Transformer for offline meta-RL that learns task representations
entry.summary: Decision Transformer with Task-Aware Representations for Offline Meta-Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes CoTA-DT, a Decision Transformer-based framework for offline meta-reinforcement learning. It learns task representations by combining contrastive learning, alignment with natural-language task descriptions, a task-conditioned world model, and a task-conditioned Q function, then uses them to condition the policy. The authors report that it consistently outperforms prior methods across offline meta-RL benchmarks, especially in zero-shot generalization.

entry.title: Controlling how action heads co-adapt to anisotropic VLM representations
entry.summary: Controlling Action-Head Co-Adaptation to VLM Representation Anisotropy arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies how a downstream action head adapts to the geometry of a pretrained vision-language model in vision-language-action systems. It finds that the action model increasingly focuses its sensitivity on high-variance dimensions of the VLM outputs. The authors propose AdaIE, a parameter-free method that reweights pretrained representations during training, which improves success rates on simulation and real-world manipulation benchmarks.

entry.title: Studying adversarial generative engine optimization through implicit brand injection
entry.summary: Characterizing Adversarial GEO via Implicit Brand Injection arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines how a brand can be promoted in generative search answers by inserting a single, contextually blended mention into a web article. The authors propose Implicit Brand Injection (IBI), a multi-agent framework that selects insertion points, rewrites sentences, verifies edits, and chooses final candidates. They evaluate it on IBIBench, a benchmark of 1,000 articles and 60 synthetic brands across 12 domains. IBI preserves semantics better and improves retrieval, reaching up to 82.2% Hit@10 and 62.7% brand mention rate.

entry.title: WASP-Mem: Agents Organize Procedural Memory, Humans Focus on Diagnosis
entry.summary: WASP-Mem: Let Agent Organize Procedural Memory. Human Spend Effort on Diagnosis arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces WASP-Mem, a method that lets LLM agents distill execution traces and feedback into persistent, interlinked wiki pages for continual learning. On the TheAgentCompany benchmark, it raises checkpoint pass rates by 4.6-6.1% over the strongest compared baseline across three models while requiring 57-61% less storage. The study finds that prescriptive human-defined schemas hurt performance, and a single round of human diagnosis outperforms four rounds of self-judgment by 7.0-10.9%.

entry.title: Effect of Nonlinear Registration on Longitudinal PET Analysis in a Rat Stroke Model
entry.summary: Evaluating the Impact of Nonlinear Registration on Longitudinal PET Analysis in a Rodent Stroke Model arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This study compares two pipelines for aligning rat PET images to a common atlas: affine-only registration and a two-stage affine plus nonlinear registration. It uses 32 longitudinal [18F]-FDG PET scans from 8 rats across 4 timepoints. The nonlinear stage yielded higher Dice similarity coefficients on every scan, with a significant gain at the rat level. However, group-level linear mixed-effects maps differ between the two pipelines in the size, number and location of suprathreshold clusters, showing that the registration choice can change downstream interpretation.

entry.title: Dory1.0-4B: A 4B-Parameter Language Model That Adjusts Depth via Looping
entry.summary: Dory1.0-4B: A Looped Normalized-GPT arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces Dory1.0-4B, a 4-billion-parameter language model whose recurrent block can be applied a variable number of times, so one checkpoint serves different compute budgets. It is built on a normalized Transformer backbone and pre-trained on 6 trillion tokens, then post-trained with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Increasing the loop count improves accuracy, most notably on coding, agentic, and long-context benchmarks.

entry.title: When Music Needs Meaning: Semantic Communication for the Musical Metaverse
entry.summary: When Music Needs Meaning: Semantic Communication as a Transformative Enabler for the Musical Metaverse arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines the communication demands of the Musical Metaverse, where distributed musicians, audiences, sound engineers, and AI agents interact through synchronized audio, visual, kinematic, and haptic streams. The authors argue that semantic communication, which transmits musically meaningful information rather than raw samples, can address its latency, synchronization, and bandwidth needs. They propose a three-pillar framework covering semantics extraction, semantic-aware orchestration, and cross-modal synchronization, along with a semantic-first reference architecture. The paper presents the Musical Metaverse as a demanding use case for 6G semantic communication.

entry.title: FlagRot: selective rotation to make 2-bit memory caches for AI models more accurate
entry.summary: FlagRot: Selective Rotation for Low-Bit KV Caches arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Long-context AI inference is limited by the KV cache, which 2-bit encoding could shrink about sixfold if the error stays small. Prior methods rotate keys before quantization, but the authors find rotation does not always help. FlagRot stores each 32-channel group either rotated or unrotated, choosing whichever has lower calibrated attention error, and rotates the query at read time. At 2.5 bits per value it lowers KIVI's KL divergence across twelve models and improves RULER at 128k tokens and LongBench v1 scores.

entry.title: A guideline-based multi-agent system for personalized exercise prescriptions from clinical and wearable data
entry.summary: A Guideline-Grounded Multi-Agent Framework for Personalized Exercise Prescription from Clinical and Wearable Data arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents FITTER, a multi-agent framework that combines clinical data, wearable device data, and condition-specific exercise guidelines to generate personalized FITT-VP exercise prescriptions. It applies deterministic safety auditing and repair to correct violations that can be checked against rules. Evaluated on data from 400 All of Us participants against five LLM comparators, FITTER achieved 98.5% safety-constraint compliance, compared with 75.8-85.8% for the comparators. Clinicians also reviewed 80 prescriptions.

entry.title: SLATE: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Testing AI Agents' Long-Task API Selection in E-commerce
entry.summary: SLATE: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Long-Horizon API Selection in E-commerce Tool Use arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces SLATE, a benchmark that tests how well LLM agents select and chain the right APIs from a library of about 1,000 e-commerce tools over long, multi-step procedures. It uses a deterministic simulator with recorded outputs and scores agents by whether they reach all required task outcomes. In experiments with six open models ranging from 3B to 12B parameters, the best model completed only 5.0% of tasks.

entry.title: A fast mean-field method for moving multi-agent formations using one shared neural controller.
entry.summary: Rapid Mean-Field Formation Transport with a Shared-Representation Neural Fokker-Planck Controller arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes a mean-field formation transport method for large-scale multi-agent systems that has low online computational cost. A single shared parameterized nonlinear map approximates both the density and the control. Its parameters are optimized using Fokker-Planck residuals, formation-matching costs, and control effort. Experiments show a favorable accuracy-runtime trade-off and lower transport error than classical feedback baselines.

entry.title: Measuring model-specific alignment drift in LLM-based opinion dynamics
entry.summary: Measuring Model-Specific Alignment Drift in LLM-Based Opinion Dynamics arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper uses large language model agents as synthetic participants in opinion-dynamics experiments, letting them discuss a contested policy issue over repeated rounds. Stances are measured with a fixed psychometric instrument that is independent of the dynamics model. Without peer input, agents keep their assigned side throughout, so the loss of alignment under discussion is interaction-induced and varies by model. The authors conclude that the choice of LLM is a key validity variable for social simulation.

entry.title: Must AI Spell It Out? Understanding Alerts in Time-Critical Tasks
entry.summary: Must AI Spell It Out? Pragmatic Comprehension of Alerts in a Time-Critical Task arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This study examines whether people can use their prior knowledge to understand incomplete alerts from a machine in a time-critical monitoring task. In a preregistered experiment (N=114), a pragmatic planner that reasons over a model of the listener's knowledge was compared with a baseline that describes problems fully in onset order. Participants resolved underspecified alerts almost as reliably as fully specified ones, responded sooner, detected more problems, and rated the pragmatic assistant helpful more often without reporting higher mental demand.

entry.title: One Mistake, Three Layers: Persistence Rules for Layer-wise Probing
entry.summary: One Mistake, Three Layers: Persistence Rules Under Depth Correlation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper examines how to decide the layer at which a signal first becomes decodable from frozen network representations. It shows that a common rule requiring three consecutive layers above threshold produces false early onsets when neighboring layers are correlated, and proposes an estimator calibrated by permuting labels within each evaluation unit. Applied to pocket information in a co-folding model, it also reports that a public checkpoint loads with 128 trunk parameters missing.

entry.title: Stacking-Based Weighting for Large Language Bayes Under Model Misspecification
entry.summary: Stacking-Based Weighting for Large Language Bayes in M-Open Settings arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes a stacking-based method for combining candidate models in Large Language Bayes (LLB), which turns natural language problem descriptions into probabilistic programs. Instead of Bayesian model averaging by marginal likelihood, the method chooses model weights by optimizing predictive performance. Because leave-one-out predictions are intractable in latent-variable models, the authors derive a tractable ELBO-based stacking objective. On real-world inference tasks, it matches Bayesian model averaging in predictive performance while producing more dispersed weights.

entry.title: Ermakov-based parameter-free embeddings for physics-informed neural networks
entry.summary: Ermakov--Based embeddings as a parameter-free layer for physics-informed neural networks arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes embedding the classical Ermakov-Pinney scale function into the input layer of a physics-informed neural network as a parameter-free feature, for evolution equations with time-dependent coefficients. The scale function is obtained in closed form from the initial data via an exact moment identity, requiring no auxiliary network or knowledge of the solution. The authors compare three problem families and find that each requires a different component of the construction, with the benefit varying across them.

entry.title: Sampling interventional outcome distributions with orthogonal MMD flow
entry.summary: Sampling Interventional Distributions with Orthogonal MMD Flow arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes IMMD-Flow, a particle-based method that represents a target interventional outcome distribution through its kernel mean embedding and samples from it via MMD gradient flow. The kernel embedding estimator is doubly robust and Neyman-orthogonal, and the method supports both hard and soft interventions. It extends to high-dimensional image outcomes using frozen encoders. On image benchmarks, it matches or improves on state-of-the-art generative approaches while being significantly faster.

entry.title: A conditional adversarial diffusion model that predicts how diabetic macular edema patients will respond to anti-VEGF eye injections.
entry.summary: A Novel Conditional Adversarial Diffusion Model for High-Fidelity OCT-to-OCT Image Translation and Precise Anti-VEGF Therapy Response Prediction in Diabetic Macular Edema arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes a conditional adversarial diffusion framework that synthesizes post-treatment OCT eye images from baseline scans to estimate a patient's initial response to anti-VEGF therapy. It was trained with 5-fold cross-validation on a US cohort of 127 patients and externally validated on an Iranian cohort of 44 patients. At the 10% and 20% central subfield thickness reduction thresholds, it achieved the highest balanced accuracy among the compared methods in both cohorts.

entry.title: P²-MOPD: Speeding Up Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation Using Parameter Priors
entry.summary: P²-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies multi-teacher on-policy distillation, which transfers expert abilities to a student model by supervising the trajectories the student generates. The authors treat the linear combination of student and expert parameters as one differentiable model and propose P²-MOPD, which jointly optimizes the mixing coefficients and student weights under the same distillation objective. Experiments across four domains at 1.7B and 4B scales show faster and more balanced recovery than MOPD, with the 1.7B model reaching 94.7% average recovery versus 80.9% for MOPD.

entry.title: Do Point Cloud Models Still Need Built-In Rotation Invariance? A Robustness Benchmark
entry.summary: Do We Still Need Rotation-Invariant Architectures? A Statistical Robustness Benchmark for Point Cloud Classification arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper benchmarks 10 point cloud classification architectures under pose, noise, and occlusion perturbations across 5 domains, using confirmatory hypothesis tests. Rotation-invariant architectures show the best pose robustness but rank among the lowest on noise robustness in 4 of 5 domains. The authors retrain all models with a simple invariance loss and evaluate them on ModelNet40-C, finding that invariance training reliably improves only the corruption types it targets. At matched training budget, the best standard backbone and the best rotation-invariant architecture perform on par on unseen corruptions.

entry.title: Weighting Chain-of-Thought and Answers When Fine-Tuning Small Medical Language Models
entry.summary: Balancing Chain-of-Thought and Answer Supervision for Small Language Models on Medical Question Answering arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper compares two supervised fine-tuning methods for small language models (up to 9B parameters) used in local medical question answering. Uniform-across-Sequence weights the full reasoning-and-answer sequence equally, while Segment-weighted weights the reasoning and answer losses separately. Evaluated on multiple-choice and free-text medical QA, the study finds neither method is universally best: Segment-weighted generally does better on multiple-choice, and Uniform-across-Sequence performs best on free-text.

entry.title: A research sprint with AI: the AI worked, but the research didn't
entry.summary: We Ran a Research Sprint With AI. The AI Worked. The Research Didn't arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper argues that individual productivity gains from generative AI research tools do not guarantee better team research, and that how AI use is structured matters as much as access. Through a 100-minute sprint pilot with twelve researchers in three independent teams, the authors observed two recurring patterns: a consumption bottleneck and AI-induced research silos. They propose a Human-AI-Human collaboration framework and seven falsifiable design hypotheses for follow-up study.

entry.title: Camera, radar and LiDAR fusion using projected point clouds for multi-task learning
entry.summary: Camera Radar LiDAR Fusion via Point-Cloud Projection for Multi-Task Learning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes an early fusion architecture that combines camera images with perspective-view point cloud data from HD radar and LiDAR for autonomous driving perception. The model is trained to detect vehicles and segment free drivable space simultaneously. Experiments on the RADIal dataset show that front-view fusion of point clouds and camera images outperforms recent standalone and fusion models.

entry.title: Fixing Coordinates, Class-Wise NMS and Null Returns for Sim2Real V2X LiDAR Detection
entry.summary: Coordinate Frame Recovery, Per Class NMS and Null Return Modelling for Sim2Real V2X LiDAR Detection arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper describes an entry to the V2X-Real track of the UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge, where a 3D detector is trained only on synthetic point clouds and tested on real roadside LiDAR. The authors report three corrections: recovering a coordinate frame mismatch, using per-class non-maximum suppression so nearby pedestrians are not suppressed, and modelling null returns encoded as (0, 0, 0). The final combined score is 0.7457.

entry.title: Geometric Refinement and Distributional Alignment for Sim2Real Roadside LiDAR Detection
entry.summary: Geometric Refinement and Distributional Alignment for Sim2Real Roadside LiDAR Detection arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper describes an entry to the LUMPI track of the UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge, where a 3D object detector is trained only on synthetic data and tested on unseen real roadside LiDAR. The synthetic point clouds are also scored for distributional realism. Starting from a PointPillars baseline, the authors report gains from a parameter-free geometric refinement, repairing a faulty post-processing rule, and analytically examining the realism metrics. The final combined score is 0.4793.

entry.title: Labtune: Treating lab structure and information sharing as experimental variables in LLM-agent research
entry.summary: Labtune: Treating Lab Organization and Information Sharing as Experimental Variables in LLM-Agent Discovery arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces Labtune, an open framework for bounded research workflows where users choose lab organization, communication policy, model settings and budget. It offers six editable organizational designs and lets information sharing vary independently, with the controller enforcing sharing at phase barriers. The work is an idea and system-description paper without benchmark results, aiming to make these design choices configurable and measurable.

entry.title: Speeding Up the FastDEC Clustering Algorithm on GPUs
entry.summary: Accelerating FastDEC Clustering Algorithm with GPUs arXiv · Nov 3, 2026FastDEC is a clustering method based on dominance-based density estimation, but its exact nearest-neighbor search and dominance component processing are computationally costly. This paper presents SymWarp-FastDEC, a GPU-accelerated version that uses SymTrikNN, an exact self-k-NN kernel exploiting search symmetry, and WP-DC, a warp-parallel dominance component reduction algorithm. On the evaluated benchmarks it produces clustering outputs identical to the original FastDEC and achieves about 1.7x to 4.9x higher end-to-end performance than a FAISS-based variant.

entry.title: CoReMatch: Real-Time Robot Feature Matching via Recurrent Continuous Coordinate Refinement
entry.summary: CoReMatch: Recurrent Continuous Coordinate Refinement for Real-Time Robotic Feature Matching arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents CoReMatch, a feature matching method that refines image correspondences directly in continuous coordinate space instead of predicting discrete confidence maps on fixed grids. A Deep Aggregated Transformer captures global context and iteratively updates correspondence coordinates at a coarse stage, followed by a lightweight regression head for finer localization. On indoor and outdoor benchmarks, CoReMatch outperforms Efficient LoFTR in accuracy while running more than 10 times faster on embedded edge hardware.

entry.title: Beyond Division of Labor: How Roles Shape Feedback and Recovery in Multi-Agent Systems
entry.summary: Beyond Division of Labor: How Roles Shape Feedback and Recovery in Multi-Agent Systems arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how role instructions affect multi-agent LLM teams, comparing role-structured and role-free teams after a failed first answer. Agents, topology, call budget, and evaluator are held constant while only roles vary, using experiments on Omni-MATH and SciBench. Roles leave first-pass accuracy largely unchanged, but a role-structured Reviewer often withholds approval, so the team submits less and receives fewer evaluator verdicts, which lowers recovery after failure.

entry.title: What the Memory Helps With: Measuring Task-Specific Value in Long-Term Agent Memory
entry.summary: What Is This Memory Useful For? Measuring Task-Conditioned Utility in Long-Term Agent Memory arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper measures how useful a stored agent memory is for a specific future task, rather than assigning each memory one fixed importance score. On single-call factual-recall tasks built from LongMemEval-V2 web-agent memories, memories containing the needed answer information gave larger paired gains. The authors release a public dataset of paired measurements and costs. They report that these gains do not extend to the tested software-engineering and scientific-coding benchmarks.

entry.title: Sequential audit of linked forecast errors with missing outcomes
entry.summary: Sequential auditing of connected forecast errors under partial observations arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how an auditor can selectively retrieve missing true outcomes to check whether a connected group of locations has outcomes falling outside the same side of their forecast intervals. The audit stops once the observed labels settle the question or the query budget runs out. Tested on three public graph time series, the MOMS method cut mean queries by 19.6% to 38.5% versus screened random acquisition when 30% of labels were hidden.

entry.title: Benchmark comparing Koopman-type representations for deep latent data assimilation
entry.summary: When Latent Dynamics Meet Data Assimilation: A Benchmark of Koopman-Type Representations arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper systematically compares seven representative Koopman-type methods and structural baselines across five systems, ranging from approximately periodic to strongly chaotic dynamics. It evaluates forecast and assimilation accuracy, physical state recovery, latent-trajectory behavior, and dynamical consistency. The results reveal a trade-off between representational flexibility and optimization tractability, with methods using closed-form analysis updates generally performing better and more robustly.

entry.title: EpiLoRA: Fusing Many LoRA Adapters into Low-Precision Matrix Multiplications for Serving and RL
entry.summary: EpiLoRA: Fusing Many LoRA Adapters into Low-Precision GEMMs for Serving and RL arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents EpiLoRA, a plugin for the vLLM engine that fuses LoRA adapter computations into the final stage of low-precision base-model matrix multiplications, reducing the cost of running adapters as separate GPU kernels. On NVIDIA Hopper GPUs, the authors report up to 24% lower time per token for single-adapter decoding than vLLM's fastest configuration, and higher adapter-kernel throughput with many tenants. The approach also enables LoRA reinforcement-learning training directly on the engine's FP8 weights without a 16-bit copy.

entry.title: Limits of Neural CDE Information with Sparse Observations
entry.summary: The Information Limits of Neural Controlled Differential Equations Under Sparse Observations arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies the uncertainty in Neural Controlled Differential Equations when observations are sparse, since many continuous paths can fit the same data and yield different terminal states. For planar drivers with bounded speed, it gives a leading-order zonotopic approximation of the compatible terminal states using feasible signed areas and transported Lie brackets. It also derives a computable, target-specific ambiguity certificate and analyzes how many measurements are needed to reduce uncertainty, with synthetic experiments testing the certificate.

entry.title: ProofPaths: An AI Agent Framework for Assessing Student Reasoning
entry.summary: ProofPaths: An AI Agent Framework for Assessing Student Reasoning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces ProofPaths, an AI agent framework that combines rubric-based grading with individualized, interactive interviews to assess whether students understand the reasoning behind their submissions. Multiple grading agents evaluate work against instructor guidance, critique each other, and revise their judgments, with their scores determining the grade and feedback.
