An interview agent asks students to justify steps in their work and generates follow-up questions based on their answers. The system stores grading reviews and interview transcripts, and instructors can inspect them and override grades.

entry.title: Embedding Semantic Entropy: NLI-free uncertainty estimation via geometry-aware clustering for language models
entry.summary: Embedding Semantic Entropy: NLI-Free Semantic Uncertainty Estimation with Geometry-Aware Clustering arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Large language models often produce fluent but incorrect answers, so estimating their uncertainty matters. This paper proposes Embedding Semantic Entropy, which replaces entailment-based clustering with K-Medoids clustering in semantic embedding space and uses dynamic cluster selection. The method is evaluated on five datasets and four models, showing competitive AUROC and AUARC results.

entry.title: INSIGHT-HPC: An Interpretable System Intelligence for Global HPC Telemetry
entry.summary: INSIGHT-HPC: An Interpretable System Intelligence for Global HPC Telemetry arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents INSIGHT-HPC, a multi-plane anomaly-detection architecture for telemetry from high-performance computing clusters. It combines statistical, workload-aware, and physics-guided evidence to turn minute-level observations into de-duplicated fault episodes with operator-facing explanations. On production telemetry with weak labels and controlled fault injections, it reports a precision of 0.913, recall of 0.817, F1 of 0.862, and AUROC of 0.896, outperforming all evaluated baselines.

entry.title: Learning Almost Complex and Complex Structures: numerical searches for complex structures on spheres and sphere products.
entry.summary: Learning Almost Complex and Complex Structures arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper numerically constructs almost complex and complex structures on spheres and products of spheres up to real dimension six. Almost complex structures are parametrised by a global matrix field in Euclidean space, and polynomial features and neural networks are used to search for them. Nine examples pass the numerical admissibility checks, while S^4 is rejected. Learned complex structures on S^2×S^2, S^3×S^1, S^3×S^3 and S^5×S^1 have Nijenhuis norms below 10^-9, and direct constructions in torus-fibred coordinates are given for S^6, S^4×S^2 and S^4×T^2.

entry.title: EvoGroup: A self-evolving framework for group agents working in shared contexts
entry.summary: EvoGroup: A Self-Evolving Harness for Group Agents in Shared Contexts arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes EvoGroup (EvoG), a self-evolving harness for group agents that starts from a minimal six-tool setup and adapts through interaction with shared context. On a held-out split of EverMemBench, pass@1 rises from 71.07% to 89.58%, surpassing self-evolving memory systems and human-designed harnesses, including Claude Code at 85.83%. The frozen harness also generalizes to the unseen GroupMemBench, outperforming memory baselines and human-designed harnesses.

entry.title: ExaTune: Exhaustive Mapping of Hyperparameter Performance Landscapes at Scale
entry.summary: ExaTune: Exhaustive Hyperparameter Landscape Exploration at Scale arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents ExaTune, an open-source HPC system that exhaustively evaluates every point on a discretized hyperparameter grid using K-fold cross-validation to produce hyperparameter landscape maps. It computes five landscape metrics, including spatial autocorrelation, ruggedness, local optima density, fitness-distance correlation, and variance-based parameter importance. The authors release eight complete landscape maps covering 285,080 configurations across five model families. They report that Bayesian optimization, Optuna, Hyperband, and Random Search at standard trial budgets miss instability regions, secondary optima, and parameter interactions visible in the full landscapes.

entry.title: Dr. No: steering model features so vision-language models abstain when evidence is lacking
entry.summary: Dr. No: Feature Steering for Abstention in Vision-Language Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Large foundation models often answer even when visual or textual evidence is insufficient, which makes them hard to trust in high-stakes settings. This paper presents Dr. No, which mines sparse autoencoder features tied to abstention and commitment and adjusts a small set of them during the prefill pass, without retraining the base model. It is tested on LLaVA-1.6 Mistral 7B across multimodal abstention benchmarks such as UNK-VQA and MM-UPD, and on AbstentionBench subsets with Qwen3.5-2B. The method achieves a better balance between correct answering and appropriate abstention than post-hoc rejection methods, but its gains are limited on absent-answer detection and multi-hop QA such as MuSiQue.

entry.title: Predictive gains, causal losses: why interventional competence cannot be learned from data alone
entry.summary: Predictive gains, causal losses: why interventional competence cannot be learned from data alone arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper argues theoretically that, for deterministic predictors, beating the best parent-only predictor on observational data requires persistent errors in intervention responses. Under the stated conditions, root-mean-square intervention-response error is bounded below by a positive constant. It further argues that correcting this error is limited by the causal hypotheses currently admitted, so reducing it further requires admitting better causal hypotheses.

entry.title: Can Rewriting Replace Long Reasoning? Effects of Compacting Reasoning History on Later Generation and Agent Cost
entry.summary: Why Pay for Long Reasoning When Rewrite Do Trick? Causal Effects of Reasoning History Compaction on Future Generation and Agent Cost arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies whether open-weight language models can reduce future reasoning-token use by rewriting their earlier reasoning into compact state records, without retraining. It compares continuations from original and compacted histories, finding that accepted compact histories usually shorten later reasoning. In software-agent deployments, compaction can lower total spending, but task quality and time including rewriting depend on the target model and compressor.

entry.title: RoboScope Kit: Unified Interfaces for Faster Embodied-AI Evaluation
entry.summary: RoboScope Kit: Unified Interfaces for Fast and Scalable Embodied-AI Evaluation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents RoboScope Kit, which wraps each model as a unified Policy class and each simulation benchmark as an adapter, leaving the benchmark's own evaluation rules and scoring unchanged. It schedules simulator workers and policy replicas as separate pools, sized from measured probes, and shards work deterministically across GPUs. On LIBERO-Long it evaluates 500 episodes 4.45 times faster than the official StarVLA evaluator with equivalent success rates. On RoboTwin Easy, four GPUs finish 500 episodes in 14.4 minutes, 25.04 times faster than the single-GPU baseline, with identical success outcomes and terminal steps.

entry.title: LaplaceDiag: Locating Faults via Changes in Learned Actuator Effects
entry.summary: LaplaceDiag: Fault Diagnosis through Changes in Learned Actuator Effects arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces LaplaceDiag, a data-driven method that uses changes in actuator effects to narrow the search for faulty equipment. It learns a healthy plant model with LaplaceNet, a neural network operating in Laplace space, separating nonlinear history-based prediction from an explicit matrix describing how actuators affect sensors. Comparison with a healthy reference detects changes and generates actuator-related diagnostic hypotheses, supporting both online and offline diagnosis. The authors report evaluating the method on two datasets.

entry.title: Steering AI-generated antibody designs with uncertainty, tested in a lab-in-the-loop setup
entry.summary: Probabilistic Steering of Generative Priors for Lab-in-the-Loop Antibody Optimization arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes merging the two usual stages of antibody development, discovery and refinement, into one process. A generative structure model is gradually handed over to iterative optimization, with the switch guided by the posterior uncertainty of a probabilistic surrogate model. The authors report better optimization efficiency when data is scarce, along with more diverse optimized molecules.

entry.title: PianoBench: A Benchmark Testing Whether Language Models Can Perceive and Reason About Piano Music
entry.summary: PianoBench: Evaluating Musical Perception and Reasoning in Language Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces PianoBench, a benchmark that asks language models to reason about piano performances using both audio and symbolic transcript inputs. It is built from a new dataset of over 20,000 hours of music interleaved with spoken commentary from piano instruction videos. Open audio-language models reach at most 52.8% accuracy, while frontier models given text transcripts reach up to 93.2%.

entry.title: Measuring How Varied Language Model Responses Are Using Conditional Mutual Information
entry.summary: A Conditional Mutual Information Analysis of Response Variety in Language Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper analyzes the variety of responses generated by large language models using an entropy-based approach built on conditional mutual information. It defines three limiting behaviors, arbiter, independent, and neutral (deterministic), which span from no to maximal mutual information. The authors give examples of each and suggest applications in temperature analysis, language analysis, prompt compression, and knowledge graphs.

entry.title: Low-Rank Hierarchical Merging for Efficient Long-to-Short Reasoning
entry.summary: Low-Rank Hierarchical Merging for Efficient Long-to-Short Reasoning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes LHM, a training-free framework that merges long chain-of-thought models with base models to keep strong reasoning while producing concise outputs. It replaces first-order heuristics with lightweight second-order curvature estimates to assign layer-adaptive merge coefficients. Tested on six math benchmarks with 1.5B and 7B models, LHM reports over 4% higher accuracy than ACM-TIES and ORCA and up to 93.1% shorter outputs than the long-CoT model.

entry.title: El Agente Fármaco: A Scalable AI Scientist for Drug Discovery
entry.summary: El Agente Fármaco: A Scalable AI Scientist for Drug Discovery arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces El Agente Fármaco, an AI scientist that uses large language models to turn everyday-language drug discovery goals into scalable computational screening workflows. It relies on a shared memory, Fármaco Atlas, which stores molecules, structures, and results together with their provenance. In a retrospective comparison and a 22-task benchmark, the agent reportedly performed competitively against an expert-led campaign and baseline tool-calling approaches.

entry.title: Rethinking next-visit diagnosis prediction with retrieval-memory multi-agent adjudication
entry.summary: Rethinking Next-Visit Diagnosis Prediction Beyond Aggregate Metrics: Retrieval--Memory Multi-Agent Adjudication arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines predicting the diagnoses a patient will have at their next clinical visit from electronic health records. The authors propose an evaluation framework that considers diagnosis set distribution and temporal transitions, and compare rule-based, LLM, retrieval, memory, and multi-agent approaches. They find that repeating the last visit's diagnoses outperforms most LLM-based methods overall. They then introduce LONGINUS, a framework combining retrieved patient record evidence with structured patient trajectory memory, evaluated on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV.

entry.title: BEND 2.0: A benchmark testing the skills needed to design DNA
entry.summary: BEND 2.0: Benchmarking the Capabilities Needed to Design DNA arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces BEND 2.0, a benchmark for DNA language models that tests how well they predict the effects of DNA changes and whether those predictions can guide sequence design. Across eight tasks built on five experimental datasets, model choice and how representations are accessed both affect performance. Linear readouts on frozen representations can match or exceed models' native outputs, and functional post-training substantially improves capabilities.

entry.title: 3D dark matter map of the COSMOS-Web field from JWST, using generative AI priors
entry.summary: 3D dark matter map of the JWST COSMOS-Web field using diffusion-based generative priors arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper reconstructs the three-dimensional dark matter distribution in the 0.54 square degree COSMOS-Web field using deep James Webb Space Telescope imaging. It combines a weak lensing forward model with a diffusion-based Bayesian generative prior learned from cosmological simulations, producing a posterior distribution across 20 lens planes out to redshift about 2. The reconstruction separates overlapping structures and recovers non-Gaussian matter structure across several spatial scales.

entry.title: FlowRig: Unified Skeleton Generation for 3D and 4D Meshes via Flow Matching
entry.summary: FlowRig: Unified Skeleton Generation for 3D and 4D Meshes via Flow Matching arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes MoTWorld, a framework that uses flow matching to generate skeletons for both static 3D meshes and dynamic 4D mesh sequences. It produces temporally aligned skeletons for an entire sequence in one feedforward pass and allows control over bone count. The model also supports uncertainty estimation and masking-based interpolation and forecasting. Training starts from large-scale 3D rigging data and adapts to mid-scale 4D mesh-skeleton data. Experiments report strong 3D rigging performance and consistent 4D reconstruction and prediction results.

entry.title: Metadata-conditioned audio transformers for adaptive respiratory sound classification
entry.summary: Metadata-Conditioned Audio Transformers for Adaptive Respiratory Sound Classification arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses how recording device, auscultation site, and patient characteristics introduce variability in respiratory sound classification that is unrelated to pathology. It proposes metadata-conditioning mechanisms for the Audio Spectrogram Transformer, progressing from gated residual fusion to FiLM, and introduces two variants, TAFiLM and SoftFiLM. On the ICBHI benchmark, all conditioning strategies improve results, with SoftFiLM reaching 64.11% on the 4-class task (+3.94% over baseline) and 72.40% on the 2-class task.

entry.title: Multi-layer Indexer: a method to speed up sparse attention in long-context language models by reusing token selections across layers.
entry.summary: Multi-layer Indexer: Overlapping Selection and Attention in DeepSeek Sparse Attention arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper addresses the decoding bottleneck in DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA), where a lightning indexer scanning the full cache dominates time at long context. Because adjacent layers select nearly the same tokens, the proposed Multi-layer Indexer lets a layer reuse the previous indexer layer's selection, so each indexer runs concurrently with attention, with no retraining or new weights. Combined with IndexCache, it decodes faster at equal retention on DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5, while its LongBench, RULER and LongBench v2 accuracy stays within a few percentage points of IndexCache.

entry.title: Benchmarking general-purpose language models for predicting alloy properties, using a distance measure to quantify out-of-distribution data
entry.summary: Quantifying out-of-distribution data severity with Wasserstein distances: benchmarking large language models for alloy property prediction arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper compares general-purpose large language models such as Gemini and DeepSeek with domain-specific materials models for predicting properties of titanium, steels, high-entropy alloys, and aluminum. The general models outperformed SteelBERT, MatSciBERT, and SciBERT, and feeding a prior model's numerical estimates into the prompts let the LLMs exceed that prior model's accuracy. The authors also report that data quality matters more than quantity, with 5% of highly similar reference data performing close to the full training set.

entry.title: VagueBench: Testing Embodied Agents' Reliance on Surrounding Context
entry.summary: VagueBench: Benchmarking the Robustness of Embodied Agents on Ambient Context Illusions arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper identifies the Ambient Context Illusion, where embodied agents fail when non-essential contextual details are removed from instructions while the task meaning stays the same. The authors built VagueBench, a benchmark of 1,303 instruction pairs in the AI2-THOR simulator, organized into a taxonomy of four categories and nine subtypes. Testing six state-of-the-art agents, they found task success rates dropped by a relative 19.65% and empty plan rates rose by a relative 54.10%. The authors also report the same effect in real-world robotic systems.

entry.title: How injected noise shapes diffusion model generalization
entry.summary: The role of injected noise in diffusion model generalization arXiv · Nov 2, 2026Diffusion models trained on different datasets can produce very similar samples from the same noise input, suggesting they learn a generalized data distribution. This study examines the noise injected during sampling and finds it plays an important role in either sustaining or breaking this strong generalization effect. The authors further show that sample similarity is most sensitive to changes in injected noise during the stage where broad structure has formed but the specific sample identity is not yet determined.

entry.title: Language models may gain from domain-specific built-in learning biases
entry.summary: Language Models Can Benefit from Domain-Specific Inductive Biases arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper trains small language models from scratch on subsets of pretraining data such as web text, code, and mathematics. It replaces standard transformer activation functions with learned splines tuned on specific datasets to change the model's inductive biases. The tuned variants improve training efficiency or generalization on all seven tested datasets, but the gains are often domain-specific, with architectures tuned on one domain frequently performing poorly on others.

entry.title: Improving Stock Market Information Retrieval Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entry.summary: Enhancing Stock Market Information Retrieval with Retrieval-Augmented Generation arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system that combines retrieval and generative methods to produce more accurate and relevant responses to stock market queries. The authors evaluate it on 100 stock market-related queries using ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, and ROUGE-L scores, which measure similarity to reference texts, and report high scores. The system's average response time is 1.16 seconds.

entry.title: CaRe-KT: Continuity-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Knowledge Tracing
entry.summary: CaRe-KT: Continuity-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Knowledge Tracing arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes CaRe-KT, a framework for knowledge tracing that estimates a learner's evolving knowledge state from interaction histories. It uses an Evidence-Graph Cache to build query-specific subgraphs that retrieve other learners' historical trajectories, and an attention mechanism that combines retrieval relevance with learned query-evidence compatibility. The authors report that CaRe-KT outperforms strong baselines across five benchmarks and remains robust under sparse-history and cold-start conditions.

entry.title: EvoMemState: A state-centric memory framework for personal LLM agents
entry.summary: EvoMemState: Evolving Memory State for Personal Agents arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents EvoMemState, a framework that gives LLM agents long-term memory by tracking more than isolated facts. It adds Relational States describing how facts remain valid and relate to each other, and a Reasoning State, generated through reinforcement learning, that determines how facts apply to the current request. Experiments on long-term dialogue and memory-use benchmarks report gains in retrieval completeness and memory-grounded response accuracy over existing memory systems.

entry.title: Region-consistent open-set object detection that avoids conflicting known/unknown labels on the same object
entry.summary: Beyond Proposals: Region-Consistent Open-Set Object Detection arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper addresses open-set object detection, where overlapping proposals for the same object receive contradictory known or unknown predictions. It reframes the task as object-centric semantic inference and proposes OCSI-Net, which groups correlated proposals into region clusters and infers region-level semantics from aggregated evidence. A geometry-aware uncertainty mechanism is also introduced to stabilize training near open-set boundaries. The authors report state-of-the-art results across multiple benchmarks, with the harmonic mean of known and unknown detection improved by an average of 6.83% over the second-best method.

entry.title: Reasoning is topologically simple
entry.summary: Reasoning is topologically simple arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes and examines the hypothesis that reasoning text has a simpler word co-occurrence topology than non-reasoning text, and that higher-quality reasoning has simpler topology than lower-quality reasoning. The authors discuss and test applications of this idea to AI safety and AI evaluation.

entry.title: RATSIFT: A Transformer That Forecasts Solar Irradiance at Adjustable Time Resolutions
entry.summary: RATSIFT: Resolution-Adaptive Transformer for Solar Irradiance Forecasting and Temporal Downscaling arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents RATSIFT, a Transformer-based model that performs solar irradiance forecasting and temporal downscaling at the same time. It accepts inputs at arbitrary resolutions and produces outputs at any resolution found in its training data, using both global and local context. A genetic algorithm is used to tune hyperparameters with less computation than exhaustive grid search. On real data from Dallas, Texas, it achieved RMSE values of 28.785 to 32.132 W/m² for 5-minute-resolution forecasts and provided uncertainty intervals.

entry.title: SSPE: A Robust Method for Extracting Stay Points from Noisy Trajectory Data
entry.summary: SSPE: Robust Sequential Staypoint Extraction in Degraded Trajectory Data arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents SSPE, an algorithm for extracting stay points from location trajectories affected by spatial noise and long signal dropouts. It replaces fixed spatial anchors with a dynamic centroid, uses an n-step lookahead to tolerate small coordinate drift, and applies temporal bridging to avoid splitting stationary periods during signal loss. The authors also propose an unsupervised, consensus-based method for estimating parameters without ground-truth labels. On the ExtraSensory dataset with manually verified stay points, SSPE achieves higher F1-scores and better computational efficiency than the sliding-window method in Trackintel.

entry.title: HyVox: A Hybrid Neuromorphic and Von Neumann System for Low-Power Speaker Identification
entry.summary: HyVox: Rethinking Low-Power Voice Intelligence towards Neuromorphic-von Neumann Edge Computing arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents HyVox, a hybrid system pairing a neuromorphic processor with a von Neumann microcontroller for open-set speaker identification under tight energy budgets. The neuromorphic chip runs a spiking network that produces speaker embeddings through sparse, event-driven computation, while the microcontroller manages the speaker gallery, matches queries, rejects unknown speakers, and enrolls new users. On 20 Common Voice households of unseen speakers, HyVox reaches 99.6% top-1 accuracy with 2 members and 94.9% with 20, and each 3-second inference takes 0.96 s and 1.63 mJ of dynamic energy.

entry.title: Minimal penalties that make classifier validation scores favour correct predictions
entry.summary: Minimal Superior Penalties: Characterising and Calibrating Decision-Aware Proper Scoring Rules arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper studies validation metrics used to select classifiers, requiring that every correct prediction score better than every incorrect one. It derives closed-form endpoints for the Brier and logarithmic scores and computes the infimal penalty, the smallest penalty needed to restore this superiority. The infimal penalty is smaller than previously published values, and the authors embed it in a one-parameter family whose members are strictly proper under a single tie convention.

entry.title: Guiding frozen diffusion docking models with complete donor sets
entry.summary: Complete Donor-Set Guidance for Frozen Diffusion Docking Models arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper addresses metalloprotein docking by guiding already-trained general-purpose diffusion docking models with an externally supplied complete set of ligand donor atoms, without retraining. It also proposes transferring donor identities from earlier complexes at compatible receptor sites. On 86 assessable queries, the guidance raised joint success rates for both SurfDock and DiffDock-L. The authors conclude it is a conditional correction for frozen models, with donor-source reliability and physical-quality preservation as the main barriers.

entry.title: Learning to Read Residual Images for Single-Pixel Video Reconstruction
entry.summary: Learning to read residual images for single-pixel photography arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper presents a method for reconstructing video intervals from a compact single-pixel measurement stream. It correlates the measurement residual with the coding patterns to form a residual image, lifts it through a pretrained video decoder, and uses the MGV-Flow model to reconstruct frames from this residual and preceding frames. The reported method reconstructs five frames in 1.55 seconds at 22.9 dB median PSNR, much faster than the compared baseline.

entry.title: Auditing HuggingBench: Data Quality and Training Budgets in a Model-Hub Recommendation Benchmark
entry.summary: Auditing a Model-Hub Benchmark: Data Quality, Training Budgets, and Side Information in HuggingBench arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper audits HuggingBench, a SIGIR 2025 benchmark for recommending Hugging Face resources, using data validation, replication of eleven recommendation methods, and controlled experiments with three seeds. It finds that three of four external knowledge graphs pass basic checks but violate the item-entity identity constraint, and correcting this improves knowledge-graph-based methods by up to 73% in mean Recall@10. The authors also show that the 100-epoch training budget often ends before early stopping, and that item text, unused by any reported method, is the strongest signal.

entry.title: DualClusterNet: A model for predicting users' next place visits using shared patterns
entry.summary: DualClusterNet: Personalized Pattern-Space Composition for Next-POI Recommendation arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper introduces DualClusterNet, a causal sequential recommender for next point-of-interest (POI) recommendation on location-based platforms. It combines two population-shared prototype dictionaries through soft routers and interaction layers, with a separate user-conditioned branch to retain individual preferences. Single-seed experiments on NYC and TKY datasets show competitive full-candidate ranking results, and controlled analyses support the contribution of its compositional and personalized components.

entry.title: From Logs to Faults: Reference-free fault localization for RAG pipelines, a method to find errors using logs
entry.summary: From Logs to Faults: Reference-Free Fault Localization for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Pipelines arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper presents RAGLog, a tool that detects and locates faults across the stages of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines using only execution logs, without reference answers or code instrumentation. The authors also release RAGLog Faults, a dataset of 3,134 runs from five RAG pipelines with stage-level fault labels. RAGLog is compared with Claude Code and Codex on runs with naturally occurring and injected faults. It is available as open-source software for debugging, evaluating, and monitoring RAG pipelines.

entry.title: Does the trust boundary hold over time? A long-horizon benchmark for receiver-directed federated learning
entry.summary: Does the Trust Boundary Hold over Time? A Long-Horizon Benchmark for Receiver-Directed Federated Learning arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper studies whether the trust boundary that sites in receiver-directed federated learning draw (admitting, rejecting, or abstaining on each source and model component) stays reliable over hundreds of training rounds. The authors built a benchmark with thirteen semi-synthetic sites, exact oracles for evaluated transfers, and fourteen methods run over 600 CPU rounds and 500 Qwen3-1.7B LoRA rounds. They found that the answer depends on the reference: a gate judging against a fixed starting model identified useful transfers well but admitted 29% of transfers harmful to the current model, while a gate judging against the current model admitted only 2% of harmful transfers but missed many useful ones. They also evaluate a held-out audit that decides whether final models are deployed or fall back to local training.

entry.title: EMBERS: Robustness testing for AI research agents using defect-guided fuzzing
entry.summary: EMBERS: Empirically Motivated Robustness Testing of Deep Research Systems via Defect-Guided Fuzzing arXiv · Nov 1, 2026Deep Research systems are AI agents that break down complex questions, search the web repeatedly, and combine evidence into answers. The authors analyzed 1,932 execution trajectories from three such systems and identified nine recurring defect categories across subquestion formulation, online search, and final reasoning. Based on these findings, they propose EMBERS, a fuzzing framework that generates stage-targeted test inputs to probe robustness. Across 16 framework-model-dataset settings, EMBERS achieved 3.21 times the failure-discovery throughput of the strongest baseline under identical testing budgets.

entry.title: Autonomous research driven by counterexamples, applied to excess radiated energy in a Z-pinch
entry.summary: Counterexample-driven autonomous research with application to excess radiated energy in a Z-pinch arXiv · Nov 1, 2026The paper introduces Simjecture, an open-source framework in which language-model agents test human-defined physics conjectures by searching for counterexamples and revising hypotheses. The authors used it in an 82.6-hour investigation of a long-standing Z-pinch problem, where radiated energy exceeds the kinetic energy of the imploding shell. The study finds competing effects among energy conversion, retention, and release timing.

entry.title: NepTTS-Bench: A Native-Speaker Benchmark and NepaliMOS Predictor for Nepali Speech Synthesis
entry.summary: NepTTS-Bench: Native-Speaker Benchmarking and NepaliMOS for Nepali Text-to-Speech arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper introduces NepTTS-Bench, a controlled benchmark for Nepali text-to-speech built from 205 sentences, including 77 minimal pairs, rated by 180 speakers across 6,962 ratings. It finds that the automated metric SCOREQ favors ElevenLabs while native listeners prefer Piper. The authors also present NepaliMOS, a predictor fine-tuned on the ratings, which reaches a system-level correlation of 0.90 but only 0.43 at the utterance level under leave-one-system-out evaluation.

entry.title: Physics-informed Tucker method with RKHS factors for reconstructing sparse spatiotemporal data
entry.summary: Physics-Informed Functional Tucker Method with RKHS Factors for Sparse Spatiotemporal Reconstruction arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper addresses reconstructing physical field dynamics from sparse fixed sensors and missing frames. It proposes PhysFTM, a physics-informed functional Tucker model whose mode factors live in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces and which applies PDE constraints via finite-difference residuals at off-sensor points. The model reconstructs spatial fields at observed frames and recovers missing frames through a continuous trajectory in Tucker-core space. Experiments on Allen–Cahn, Navier–Stokes, 3D heat equations, and 3D ocean reanalysis data show accurate 2D and 3D reconstruction under two missing-frame protocols.

entry.title: A compact, formula-aware summary of spreadsheets for language models
entry.summary: A Compact Formula-Aware Spreadsheet Abstraction for Large Language Models arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes a compact spreadsheet abstraction that describes large homogeneous ranges by their positions, types, R1C1 formula patterns, and selected boundary values. The abstraction is provided to a large language model before detailed content, aiming to reduce the data submitted and token consumption. The method was evaluated on 50 spreadsheet-query cases.

entry.title: Searching all reaction paths at once using Monte Carlo and neural committor methods
entry.summary: All Paths All at Once: A Quantum Monte Carlo and Neural Committor Approach to Reaction Pathway Search arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper presents tReax_expedition, an energy-only method for finding reaction pathways without potential-energy gradients, combining coupled Monte Carlo exploration, stochastic quench labelling and restrained continuation. On GFN2-xTB gas-phase reactions, sampled chain maxima for eight of nine cases differed from independently refined saddle energies by less than 0.76 kJ·mol⁻¹, while alanine dipeptide showed incomplete conformational relaxation. Neural committor learning and local straddling-pair sampling link the resulting paths to transition-region sampling.

entry.title: RSI-Dojo: Training LLM Agents to Automate Their Own Post-Training
entry.summary: Training LLM Agents to Automate LLM Post-Training with RSI-Dojo arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper introduces RSI-Dojo, a set of executable training environments that teach LLM agents to carry out post-training of models. The authors built RSI-Craft, a pipeline that converts research papers, datasets, and metrics into 281 unified model training tasks. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on filtered trajectories improved their PostTrainBench scores by 8.74 and 16.87 points.

entry.title: From Forecasting to Feedback: Testing Learned Plasma Models for Tokamak Control
entry.summary: From Forecasting to Feedback: Evaluating Learned Dynamics for Tokamak Control arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper trains action-conditioned Transformer models on data from a calibrated free-boundary Grad-Shafranov solver and optimizes PPO control policies inside these learned models. It then evaluates the policies on six reference-solver conditions. The authors find that prediction accuracy on logged trajectories does not reliably predict closed-loop control performance, and they recommend combining prediction error, episode completion, condition-level duration, and tracking quality in evaluation.

entry.title: LOLPlay: A Benchmark for Real-Time Visual Agents in League of Legends
entry.summary: LOLPlay: Benchmarking Real-Time Visual Agents in League of Legends arXiv · Oct 25, 2026This paper introduces LOLPlay, a benchmark built on the native League of Legends game with 36 champion-specific tasks covering resource management, combat, cooperation, and objectives. Agents interact through screenshots and mouse-keyboard actions, with 82 executable subgoal checks measuring partial progress. Across three models at three reasoning-effort settings, higher effort improved neither success metric over low effort for any model, and longer reasoning left fewer interaction rounds.

entry.title: Functional-group knowledge in language models is structured before it is spoken
entry.summary: Functional-Group Knowledge Is Structured in Language Models Before It Is Spoken arXiv · Oct 24, 2026This paper analyzes the internal representations of five open-source language models on prompts covering 92 molecules and 20 functional groups. Even without chemistry training, the models organize functional groups by chemical family and encode chemical differences as consistent directions, a structure that emerges in the middle layers. The base model names the correct functional group in only 58.5% of prompts yet still preserves these chemically meaningful patterns. The authors conclude that evaluating chemical language models through outputs alone can underestimate the chemical information they encode.

entry.title: MolCrew: a local system that coordinates molecular AI models for drug-like molecule design
entry.summary: A local orchestration harness for molecular design with foundation models arXiv · Oct 20, 2026The paper presents MolCrew, a locally deployable system in which a language-model orchestrator coordinates four separately trained molecular specialist models and RDKit chemistry calculations. The specialists generate structures, describe molecules, predict biological endpoints and propose edits. On 3,300 ChEBI-20 test examples it reached 96.4% exact structure recovery, versus 38.7% for published Atomas-large results. Across eight MoleculeNet datasets with scaffold splits, mean ROC AUC was 0.851, compared with 0.770 for published Atomas results.

entry.title: Learning Directional Randers Geometry for Latent-Space Exploration
entry.summary: Learning Directional Randers Geometry for Latent-Space Exploration arXiv · Oct 19, 2026The paper argues that latent spaces learned by deep networks from images lack explicit geometric structure, and that common interpolation methods assume symmetric transition costs, which cannot model one-way processes such as disease progression. The authors propose a new Finsler-Randers metric learning framework that uses direction-dependent distances so trajectories can respect monotonic sequential constraints. They demonstrate its use for interpolation and extrapolation on controlled cross-sectional datasets.

entry.title: ReVi: Recursive Recap Video Generation for Novels
entry.summary: ReVi: Recursive Recap Video Generation arXiv · Oct 19, 2026This paper studies generating a self-contained audiovisual recap video directly from a novel within a fixed viewing-time budget. The proposed ReVi is a dual-loop multi-agent framework: an Inner Loop plans story content, narration time, and shots before video generation, while an Outer Loop recursively revises both the editing policy and the meta policy governing that revision. Experiments on two evaluation sets show improved recap quality and duration compliance over representative baselines.

entry.title: A simulation-driven workflow using Bayesian optimization for early process design, illustrated with methyl acetate production
entry.summary: A Simulation-Driven Digital Workflow Integrating Bayesian Optimization for Early-Stage Process Design: A Methyl Acetate Production Case Study arXiv · Oct 18, 2026This paper presents a data-driven framework combining steady-state process simulation, surrogate modeling, and Bayesian optimization for early-stage process design. Using methyl acetate production via carbonylation of dimethyl ether as a case study, neural network surrogates were trained on 2730 simulations and used in multi-objective optimization. The results show carbon conversion yield of up to about 95% with reduced energy cost, and a nonlinear trade-off between yield and energy cost.

entry.title: Do LLMs Learn from Rewards in Context? Rethinking Reward's Role in In-Context RL
entry.summary: Imitation Dominates Reinforcement: Direct In-Context RL Is Closer to ICL Than RL arXiv · Oct 8, 2026This paper tests whether LLM agents truly perform reinforcement learning at inference time by conditioning only on raw trajectory-reward pairs in context. Controlled experiments on four benchmarks and six models show that flipping, randomizing, or removing rewards barely changes the improvement curve, while shuffled or corrupted trajectories work as well as real ones. The authors conclude that direct in-context RL is better understood as a special case of in-context learning, suggesting that input distribution and demonstrations may matter more than reward shaping for agent memory design. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report controlled experiments on four benchmarks and six models finding that reward has little effect in in-context RL, and trajectory semantics matter little either, mirroring in-context

entry.title: Do Fake Citations Count as Reward Hacking? A Pre-Registered Study
entry.summary: Are Fake Citations a Form of Reward Hacking? A Pre-Registered Study of Post-Training and Citation Cues arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper examines whether language models that have undergone post-training fabricate citations because they are rewarded for appearing scholarly. Across 900 questions in US federal case law, computational science, and medical literature, tested on twelve open-weights checkpoints and refit on fifteen, asking only for citations sharply increased fabrication in post-trained models but not base models. A length-matched control indicates the effect is specific to citations rather than verbosity. The authors conclude the reward-hacking explanation is possible but not proven.| ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that post-trained models fabricate citations far more when asked for sources, separated from verbosity by a length-matched control. entry.title: Bg-Mix: Using Image Backgrounds to Augment Electron Microscopy Data
entry.summary: Bg-Mix: On Using Image Backgrounds for Data Augmentation in Electron Microscopy Images arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes Bg-Mix, a data augmentation method that splits training images into foreground objects and backgrounds, then recombines them into new images. It targets small, sparsely labeled electron microscopy virus datasets. Tested on two datasets with two architectures, it improves box mean average precision over the baseline by +0.8 to +3.3 points.

entry.title: Tuning the Agent Harness, Not the Model, for Self-Hosted Investigative Analysis
entry.summary: Optimize the Harness, Not the Model: Fitting a Minimal Agent to a Self-Hostable LLM for Investigative Analysis arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents CLEO, a method for fitting a minimal agent harness to a fixed, self-hostable large language model. Using an expert-validated dataset, it keeps only the tools, guardrails, memory policies, and loop components that improve accuracy while staying general and auditable. On a held-out dataset, the CLEO harness reaches an 83.8% pass rate, close to the strongest out-of-the-box Claude Code SDK baseline, while being two orders of magnitude smaller.

entry.title: Same outputs, different scores: auditing the unchecked scoring rules of multimodal AI benchmarks
entry.summary: Same Outputs, Different Scores: Auditing the Unchecked Graders of Multimodal LLM Benchmarks arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper reproduces the official scoring programs of eight peer-reviewed multiple-choice benchmarks for multimodal large language models, using five open vision-language models that run on a single 16 GB GPU. It introduces a blinded human-plus-LLM-judge procedure to recover what each model actually answered. The scoring rule alone shifts accuracy by up to 22 points on identical outputs, but makes no difference when models output clean option letters. The authors argue benchmarks should report a non-compliance rate and at least two scoring rules. ★★★★ Notable: The authors audit scoring rules of eight multimodal benchmarks, reproducing official scorers on five VLMs with human-plus-LLM adjudication, reporting up to 22-point accuracy swings on identical output

entry.title: Cutting SNAP Payment Errors Cheaply with AI: A Simulation Study
entry.summary: Reducing SNAP Payment Errors at Lower Cost With AI: A Simulation Study arXiv · Nov 2, 2026New federal legislation will make states with high SNAP payment error rates pay part of benefit costs, which could exceed a billion dollars a year for some states. The study uses simulations based on public SNAP quality control data to compare risk-based preauthorization review with AI that flags specific possible discrepancies for reviewers. Under its main assumptions, risk-based review alone costs about seven times as much as combining AI flags with risk scores, and this cost advantage holds across many plausible assumptions.

entry.title: CISA: Speeding Up Long-Context Models by Retrofitting Sparse Attention
entry.summary: CISA: Retrofitting Dense Attention Models with Chunk-Indexed Sparse Attention arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper introduces Chunk-Indexed Sparse Attention (CISA), a method that adapts pretrained dense-attention language models without any gradient updates. It selects fixed-size key-value chunks using compact summaries of existing keys and shares those selections across queries in a group to cut long-context inference cost. Tests on NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano and Ultra show core attention up to 13.0x faster and end-to-end throughput up to 2.61x that of dense attention. Scores on long-context benchmarks stay close to dense attention.

entry.title: VERS: A method that steers reasoning models by editing text explanations of their activations
entry.summary: VERS: Steering Reasoning Models by Editing Their Activation Explanations arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper introduces VERS, which converts edits to natural language explanations of a reasoning model's activations into one fixed direction and adds it at paragraph breaks to shorten generated reasoning. On GSM8K it reduces generated tokens by 45.8% with an accuracy change of -0.82 percentage points. On MATH-500 it saves 31.3% of tokens at -3.05 points. On competition problems, accuracy drops at every model size.

entry.title: Using a Vision-Language Model as a Judge for Person Re-Identification
entry.summary: VLM-as-a-Judge for Person Re-Identification arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper uses a general-purpose vision-language model, applied zero-shot, to rerank short candidate lists in cloth-changing person re-identification. On the four CHIRLA scenarios it raises rank-1 accuracy in every scenario, averaging 12.9 points above the best expert model. To cut cost, the VLM is called only when the two expert models disagree at rank 1, which removes 40% of calls without a significant rank-1 drop. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that zero-shot VLM reranking improves rank-1 on all four CHIRLA scenarios, averaging 12.9 points over the best expert, with a disagreement-based gate cutting VLM calls by 40 percent

entry.title: What Drives the Sudden Solve? Diagnosing and Steering Hard-Prompt Learning in RLVR
entry.summary: What Drives the Zero-to-One Jump? Diagnosing and Steering Hard-Prompt Learning in RLVR arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies the sudden "zero-to-one" jump in which hard math prompts, unsolved for many training steps, abruptly become solved under reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. The authors measure time-to-first-positive and find that failed attempts before success show higher early generation entropy. Based on this, they propose NAPO, which integrates with GRPO by ranking negative rollouts in unsolved groups and assigning graded advantages. Under fixed rollout budgets, NAPO improves Pass@256 by 10.0 points on AIME24 and 6.6 points on AIME2025.

entry.title: Blueprint2CAD: A benchmark testing whether AI models match engineering drawings to 3D part renders
entry.summary: Blueprint2CAD: Benchmarking Foundation Models on Engineering Drawing-to-CAD Render Correspondence arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper introduces Blueprint2CAD, a benchmark that checks whether an orthographic engineering drawing and a shaded render show the same mechanical part. The dataset BlueCAD-30K is built from 29,925 CAD models. With known viewpoints, frozen encoders reach up to 65% Recall@1, falling to 43% when viewpoints are unknown, and viewpoint is identified as the main bottleneck. Six zero-shot vision-language models achieve only 0.52 to 0.67 verification accuracy.

entry.title: Agent memory as rate-limited filtering: explicit state beats long context past a reader-dependent length
entry.summary: Agent Memory as Rate-Limited Filtering: Explicit State Outlasts Long Context Beyond a Reader-Dependent Horizon arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The summary in this language did not pass the date and amount checks, so it is withheld. Check the original. ★★★★ Notable: The authors model agent memory as rate-limited recursive filtering, deriving a capacity-dependent forgetting horizon and a tight error bound, and report a reader-dependent crossover with long context.

entry.title: Concise-9B: Trimming Unneeded Thinking in a Reasoning Model
entry.summary: Concise-9B: Removing the Slack from a Reasoning Model's Thinking arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies how reasoning models keep thinking long after their answer has already formed, using Qwen3.5-9B as the base. The authors apply two rounds of on-policy rejection-sampling fine-tuning that keep the shortest correct samples, plus a small share of answer-synthesis targets, producing Concise-9B. On 8,983 held-out problems at a 32K thinking budget, it generates 0.66x the tokens of the base model with accuracy within ±1 point.

entry.title: TAC-CoT: Tool-Empowered Implicit Chain-of-Thought with Interleaved Explicit Tokens
entry.summary: TAC-CoT: Tool-Empowered Implicit Chain-of-Thought via Interleaving Explicit Tokens arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper proposes TAC-CoT, a tool-empowered adaptive implicit chain-of-thought framework for LLM agents. It replaces explicit reasoning traces with compact latent reasoning segments, keeping text tokens only for tool calls, observations, and final answers. On agentic math and QA benchmarks, it improves accuracy by up to 8.8 points and reduces model forward passes by up to 6.8x, and it also improves tool-use quality in single- and multi-tool settings.

entry.title: Answer Locally or Escalate? Post-Training Expert Routing for Real-Time Duplex Speech Models
entry.summary: Local or Escalate? Post-Training Expert Routing for Real-Time Duplex Speech Models arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper studies how a real-time full-duplex speech model can decide, at the moment it starts speaking, whether to answer a question itself or hand it to a stronger expert. The authors freeze MiniCPM-o 4.5, use only its speech input and output, and fit a logistic failure readout on its existing hidden states at the listen-to-speak transition. This gate needs no extra generation and its thresholds can be retuned without changing the duplex policy. On an internal benchmark, selective handoff improves answer accuracy by 27.1 points.

entry.title: Learning by Doing: Compiling and Curating Agent Skills from Verified Traces
entry.summary: Learning by Doing: Autonomously Compiling and Curating Agent Skills from Verified Traces arXiv · Nov 1, 2026The paper presents Zep Agent Skills, a production service that gives deployed LLM agents procedural memory. It uses only verified task attempts as evidence, compiles them into versioned Skills, and governs which Skill versions become active. Evaluated on τ³-bench banking, AppWorld, and EnterpriseOps-Gym, Skills compiled from a teacher model's traces raise the pass rates of three weaker executor models.

entry.title: Study on curiosity and cultural grounding in multi-agent LLM collaboration
entry.summary: CuriousTogether: Implications of Curiosity and Cultural Grounding in Multi-Agent LLM Interactions arXiv · Nov 1, 2026The summary in this language did not pass the date and amount checks, so it is withheld. Check the original.

entry.title: StreamClarify: A Framework That Asks for Clarification in Streaming Video Q&A
entry.summary: StreamClarify: Proactive Clarification for Grounded Streaming Video Question Answering arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper presents StreamClarify, a training-free framework for answering questions about streaming video. Before answering, it checks uncertainty and asks the user for clarification when needed, using hierarchical memory to manage visual context. The authors build StreamClarify-QA, a diagnostic benchmark of 1,837 question-answer pairs, and report improved macro accuracy across three vision-language model backbones.

entry.title: pico-WAM: Testing Whether Prediction or Trajectory Scoring Limits a Compact Robot Control Model
entry.summary: pico-WAM: Evaluating Counterfactual Prediction and Planning Error in a Compact World Action Model arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper introduces pico-WAM, a compact World Action Model with supplied physical state, and studies why it fails at control. Using 206 Push-T demonstrations and 15 training seeds, the authors compare data regimes and search settings. Counterfactual branch training improves short-horizon cost ranking and widens the coverage advantage of policy-restarted search by 4.8 percentage points. Replacing learned trajectory scores with simulator costs improves coverage, while substituting simulator states in proposal generation alone shows no detected gain.

entry.title: Self-refining prompts that help text-to-SQL tools write streaming queries
entry.summary: Self-Refining Prompt Induction for Streaming Text-to-SQL arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces Self-Refining Prompt Induction (SRPI), an offline method that turns generation failures into reusable dialect instructions while keeping model weights fixed. On Confluent Cloud Flink SQL, the same induced prompt raised mean judge scores across seven generators by 7.1 to 19.2 percentage points. A separate compression study cut prompt length by 52.7% with a small drop in score.

entry.title: Labadain-MedQA: A Tetun Medical QA Dataset for Training and Testing Language Models
entry.summary: Labadain-MedQA: A Tetun Medical QA Dataset for Fine-Tuning and Evaluating Large Language Models arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper translates two medical question-answering collections, MedAlpaca's Medical Flashcards and WikiDoc Patient Information, into Tetun using Gemini 2.5 Flash, producing 39,077 QA pairs. Human reviewers rated human translations higher than machine translations for medical accuracy and Tetun fluency, with the difference statistically significant. The authors fine-tuned Gemma and Llama models on the translated data and tested them on Tetun-translated US medical licensing exam questions, where a fine-tuned Gemma 4 12B model improved in accuracy.

entry.title: Answer Correction with Verifiable Rewards: Gemma-Family Multi-View Driving QA
entry.summary: Answer Correction with Verifiable Rewards: A Gemma-Family Study of Multi-View Driving QA arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper examines whether post-training gains on multi-camera driving question answering with Gemma models reflect changed answer selection or improved answer extraction, using archived WaymoQA evaluations. In a matched-harness comparison, a Gemma-4-12B GRPO-tuned model raised accuracy from 73.78% to 75.43%. Category breakdowns show routine perception improved by 5.93 points while safety-critical hazard prediction declined.

entry.title: A new approach to AI data analysis combining several computing engines while keeping shared context
entry.summary: AI Data Analysis: A New Approach - Multi-engine Joint State Data Analysis arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper proposes Multi-engine Joint State Data Analysis, in which an LLM handles semantics, reasoning, and orchestration while connecting Python and R machine learning kernels, SQL, and Cypher engines through a 1M context window. It organizes the approach along four dimensions and reports SQL accuracy averaging about 91% to 95% across three business databases, above a single-shot state-of-the-art baseline of 74.45%. Accuracy is also reported to converge monotonically as notes accumulate.

entry.title: ConstraintMatch: Matching Images and Text by Enforcing Consistent Regional Evidence
entry.summary: ConstraintMatch: Compositional Image-Text Matching through Constrained Regional Evidence Selection arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes ConstraintMatch, a training-free inference method for image-text matching that addresses models binding attributes to the wrong entities. It turns entity-level regional consistency into an explicit matching cost and calibrates it using spatial references from the same image. Reported gains over global matching are shown on the ARO Attribute and SugarCrepe++ attribute swap benchmarks.

entry.title: Inference First, Training Underneath: Layer-Granular LoRA Co-Serving with LayerLoom
entry.summary: Inference First, Training Underneath: Layer-Granular LoRA Co-Serving with LayerLoom arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents LayerLoom, a system that serves LLM inference and LoRA fine-tuning on the same GPUs. It schedules fine-tuning backward passes layer by layer, running only as many tasks per layer as the latency slack of in-flight requests allows, to limit impact on inference latency. On an RTX 4090 running Llama-3.1-8B under a bursty trace, it improves joint SLO attainment over prior works, with comparable or up to 12% higher fine-tuning throughput and the same training losses.

entry.title: Guarded Compression of Adam Optimizer State via Shared-Gradient Bounds
entry.summary: Guarded Compression of Adam Optimizer State with Shared-Gradient Bounds arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies compressing the two FP32 moment states of the Adam optimizer, which normally double memory relative to the weights. A coordinate's compressed moments are kept only if they reproduce the native Adam update within a tolerance for all gradients in a clipped domain; otherwise the coordinate is stored exactly. Bounding the difference between the two updates directly cuts escaped coordinates from 98.9% to 0.53% and reduces the payload to 28.3% of raw FP32 on OPT-125M. Across 120 checkpoint restores of OPT-125M and ResNet-18, guarded 8-bit log codes shrink moment payloads relative to FP32 while keeping every restored first update within tolerance.

entry.title: Telling apart GPT-5.5 Pro reasoning levels with a grammar-based benchmark
entry.summary: Distinguishing among reasoning levels of GPT 5.5 Pro via a grammar lens benchmark arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces a formal grammar-based benchmark, grounded in the theory of computation, that generates novel test data at successively higher levels of computational power. Applying it to GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.5-Pro at Medium, High, and XHigh effort, the authors report incrementally rising acceptance of the test data, showing the benchmark can detect fine-grained differences in added test-time reasoning. They also find that as test-time compute increases, model responses diverge more from human responses, which they suggest may point to a broader capability-versus-alignment conflict.

entry.title: Spatial uncertainty analysis for choosing a few hyperspectral inspection sites
entry.summary: Spatial Uncertainty Analytics for Budget-Limited Inspection of Hyperspectral Scenes arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper studies how to use the spatial pattern of classifier uncertainty to decide where a UAV or ground crew should verify land-cover maps when only a few sites can be visited. It estimates per-pixel uncertainty from disagreement among an ensemble of spectral classifiers and selects sites with a field-of-view-aware greedy coverage method. On seven benchmark scenes, the most uncertain tenth of pixels contain 2.6 to 7.9 times the error rate of the whole scene, and 15 sites cover up to 57% of the classifier's errors.

entry.title: Pixel: A Full-Stack Robot System Co-Designed for General Mobile Manipulation Learning
entry.summary: Pixel: A Co-Designed Full-Stack Robot System for Learning General-Purpose Mobile Manipulation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents Pixel, a full-stack robot system designed together across hardware, data, control, and learning to support general-purpose mobile manipulation. It combines a low-cost wheeled humanoid robot, multiple teleoperation and robot-free human data-collection interfaces, a unified whole-body controller, and a shared policy learning pipeline. A hierarchical learning stack enables language-conditioned visuomotor control and long-horizon task execution, and the system is evaluated across these components.

entry.title: Pixel-UMI: Teaching Robots Whole-Body Manipulation from Sensor-Equipped Human Demonstrations
entry.summary: Pixel-UMI: Learning Environment-Aware Whole-Body Manipulation from Sensorized Human Demonstrations arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents Pixel-UMI, a pipeline that learns environment-aware whole-body robot policies from sensorized human demonstrations. It combines Environment-Aware Retargeting, which uses scene geometry and human head and gripper trajectories to set robot posture, with Retargeting-Error-Aware Masking to handle viewpoint mismatches, and on-policy human corrections via DAgger. Evaluated on five challenging manipulation tasks, it achieves 87.0% average task progress.

entry.title: EgoActionBench: A Benchmark for Dense Action Captions in First-Person Human Videos
entry.summary: EgoActionBench: Benchmarking Dense Action Captioning for Egocentric Human Videos arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces EgoActionBench, a benchmark for evaluating fine-grained action understanding in egocentric human videos. It represents continuous manipulation as temporally localized atomic actions tied to the left hand, right hand, or both hands, with 1,407 episodes and 41,132 human-refined annotations. The authors propose an evaluation protocol that scores content, timing, and hand association, and they benchmark 20 baselines while fine-tuning two backbone models that improve EgoActionScore by 15.9 and 23.2 points.

entry.title: A neuro-symbolic method combining language models and exact cover solvers for logic puzzles.
entry.summary: From Natural Language to Exact Cover: A Neuro-Symbolic Approach to Zebra Puzzles arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes a neuro-symbolic framework for solving Zebra-style logic puzzles written in natural language. A large language model translates entities and constraints into structured tool calls that build an exact cover instance, and a symbolic solver computes the answer and provides feedback to iteratively refine the encoding. Experiments across multiple parameter scales, post-training paradigms, and model families report that this hybrid approach outperforms plain neural baselines, including chain-of-thought prompting, as well as recent neuro-symbolic methods.

entry.title: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
entry.summary: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments arXiv · Nov 3, 2026WebHarbor is a suite of 153 executable, dockerized website environments that reconstruct the visuals, content, and functional workflows of real web services under deterministic control, for stable evaluation and training of GUI web agents. The environments were built through human-agent collaboration, with 3,518 tasks covering multi-step and post-authentication workflows. A Qwen 4B-level GUI agent trained with reinforcement learning in WebHarbor generalizes to unseen tasks and performs competitively with leading open-source GUI web agents across four benchmarks.

entry.title: Larger pretraining data reverses which optimizer, Muon or AdamW, fine-tunes better.
entry.summary: Pretraining Data Scale Reverses the Muon-AdamW Fine-Tuning Gap arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper compares the Muon and AdamW optimizers after fine-tuning. It finds that once pretraining data is large enough, AdamW outperforms Muon after fine-tuning, and larger models reach this reversal at smaller token-to-parameter ratios. The authors introduce a margin-to-spread ratio to explain the trend and analyze it in language models and a linear associative memory.

entry.title: Not All Reasoning Generalizes: Learning Generalizable Reasoning Strategies in RLVR
entry.summary: Not All Reasoning Generalizes: A Case Study on Learning Generalizable Reasoning Strategies in RLVR arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) can help large language models generalize their reasoning strategies. Using a controllable equation-solving framework, the authors find that RLVR-trained models solve in-distribution tasks with step-by-step derivation but switch to brute-force enumeration under out-of-distribution shifts, causing sharp accuracy drops. Co-training with bijective inversion tasks partially restores the correct strategy and out-of-distribution accuracy, and the authors provide a theoretical analysis suggesting outcome-only RLVR implicitly favors effective reasoning strategies.

entry.title: Isekai3D SDG: A Platform for Generating Diverse Synthetic Gameplay Visual Data
entry.summary: Isekai3D SDG: A Platform for Diverse Synthetic Gameplay Visual Data arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents Isekai3D Synthetic Data Generation (SDG), a platform that simulates and captures synthetic 3D gameplay for research in vision, world models, neural graphics, and gameplay agents. It uses a two-stage workflow: first recording the world state, character movements, actions, and camera tracks during simulation, then replaying that recording to capture rendered video, images, and depth maps. Visual outputs come with frame-aligned camera, character, and action metadata.

entry.title: FADE: A factored method for scheduling prompts in online RLVR training
entry.summary: FADE: Factored Ability--Difficulty Filtering for Online RLVR Scheduling arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes FADE (Factored Ability–Difficulty Estimation), a filter that schedules prompts during online reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). It separates the policy's fast-changing skill level from each prompt's slowly changing intrinsic difficulty, estimating both with a bilinear state-space model. Across five reasoning benchmarks, two base models, and four scheduling methods under a matched rollout budget, FADE improves downstream accuracy and calibration while adding less than 0.6 ms per step.

entry.title: Decoding thoughts from EEG via hierarchical alignment of brain signals and text
entry.summary: Thought-deciphering via hierarchical EEG-to-text alignment arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies sentence-level EEG-to-text decoding, aiming to offer a communication pathway for people with communication disabilities. The authors propose a novel hierarchical alignment framework. Using context and EEG as inputs, it retrieves the sentence that was read.

entry.title: D&A: A Method That Separates Description from Assessment So Vision-Language Models Can Score Robot Task Progress Without Training
entry.summary: D&A: Decoupling Description and Assessment Enables VLMs as Zero-Shot Robotic Reward Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes D&A (Describe & Assess), a method that uses vision-language models to estimate task progress in robot videos without additional training. The model first writes an objective, task-grounded description of scene dynamics, then scores progress using explicit rubrics, which reduces confirmation bias. Because the method is purely prompt-based, its reward estimates can be used for downstream reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Strategist: Evolving AI Reasoning Strategies with Agents
entry.summary: Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces Strategist, a meta-agent that evolves inference strategies across tasks. Strategies are stored as reusable executable code blueprints in a shared library, retrieved for new tasks, tested on a small development set, and revised based on results. Across 30 benchmarks, it beats the strongest baseline on 24 and matches its average accuracy (74.7% vs. 74.0%) at 39% lower inference cost. Its strategies also transfer to unseen tasks and other models without further search. ★★★★ Notable: Meta-agent evolves reusable inference-strategy blueprints across tasks; authors report beating the strongest baseline on 24 of 30 benchmarks at 39% lower cost.

entry.title: How LLM Science Discovery Ability Traces Back to Training Data
entry.summary: Tracing the Scientific Discovery Capacity of LLMs to Their Training Data arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines what enables large language models to make scientific discoveries by tracing this capacity to their training data. The authors propose a theory in which monofacts, facts observed only once during training, determine discovery capacity. In materials science and regulatory genomics, they varied monofact rates in training sets and found that more monofacts consistently led to more discoveries across two open-weight model families. The relationship could not be explained by training-set diversity alone and could transfer across scientific domains when paired with in-domain data.

entry.title: Predicting benchmark scores from sparse, unpaired cached model responses
entry.summary: Benchmark Prediction with Sparse and Unpaired Cached Responses arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces the Product Kernel Perspective Space (PKPS), a set of low-dimensional representations of generative models built from their embedded responses. PKPS compares responses to similar, not just identical, queries, so it can use sparse and unpaired evaluation data. The authors show theoretically that PKPS-based benchmark prediction is more query-efficient than methods relying only on dense, paired data. Experiments on two large benchmark suites show PKPS-based methods outperform baselines.

entry.title: Comparing two methods for learning closure models in dynamical systems
entry.summary: Efficient Closure Learning in Dynamical Systems: A Comparison of Data-Assimilated and Embedded Approaches arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper compares two data-driven approaches for learning closure models that approximate unresolved effects in reduced dynamical systems. The study uses a synthetic epidemiological SIQR model with a nonlinear state-dependent quarantine closure to examine cost and accuracy trade-offs. Embedded training gives the strongest average accuracy, while the staged approach yields comparable qualitative behavior with moderately higher error, far fewer model evaluations, and more robust optimization.

entry.title: ufakzeka-kulak: A 31.6M-parameter Turkish speech-to-text model built and tested from scratch
entry.summary: ufakzeka-kulak: Building and Evaluating a 31.6M-Parameter Turkish Speech Recognizer from Scratch arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents ufakzeka-kulak, an open Turkish speech-to-text model with 31.6 million parameters, released under Apache-2.0. It uses a FastConformer encoder with TDT and CTC heads and was trained on 4,977 hours of audio, of which 281 hours are human-transcribed and the rest use subtitles or machine transcripts checked by a second reading of the audio. With greedy decoding it reports word error rates of 0.0921 on FLEURS Turkish and 0.0916 on Common Voice 27.0 Turkish, below Whisper base and small but above Whisper large-v3, and 0.3807 on conversational speech.

entry.title: Reviso: Video captioning that focuses on what matters most in each video
entry.summary: Reviso: Not All Visual Evidence Deserves Equal Attention in Video Captioning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents Reviso, an agentic framework for video captioning that decides what to observe and how to gather relevant visual evidence. It first builds an observation plan from a low-frame-rate preview, then selectively revisits video segments and uses tools for fine-grained inspection before generating the final caption. Experiments on four video captioning benchmarks show it outperforms the evaluated open-source baselines, and its captions better support downstream video question answering.

entry.title: DiabAgent: Toward AI Agents That Manage Physiological Control
entry.summary: DiabAgent: Toward Agentic Physiological Control arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces DiabAgent, a research suite for evaluating AI agents that control physiological states, using type 1 diabetes glucose management as the test setting. It includes the APC framework, which controls glucose through medical-device tools, the DiabetSim simulator for virtual testing, and the SweetBench benchmark of 212 glucose-control tasks. With Claude Opus 5.5, APC achieves a COGI of 73.5, compared with 71.2 for the open-source closed-loop baseline OpenAPS.

entry.title: Four Bridges: A Multi-Agent Game for Measuring AI Deception
entry.summary: Four Bridges: Measuring Deception Propensity in a Multi-Agent Game arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies deception that emerges among AI agents interacting in a multi-agent setting, without any instruction to deceive. The authors introduce the Kradle evaluation platform and Four Bridges, an information asymmetry game in which one agent knows which room is deadly. They evaluate eight frontier models, and deceptive behavior appears in every model and in 73% of all runs.

entry.title: Should Two Parties Pool Data? Private Algorithms for Assessing Compatibility
entry.summary: Should We Combine Our Data? Algorithms and Limits for Privately Assessing Data Sharing arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies whether two parties, each holding a sensitive labeled dataset, can determine if a single classifier from a hypothesis class fits both datasets without revealing their individual data points. It measures conflict by the minimum number of mistakes on the pooled data and gives private protocols under pure two-party differential privacy. Results are shown for thresholds on the real line and for halfspaces in R^d.

entry.title: Structured Visual Landscape: Generating preferred images for neurons in brains and AI networks
entry.summary: Structured Visual Landscape: Generating Preferred Representations in Biological and Artificial Neural Networks arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes a structured visual representation landscape regularized by an activation-based prior. The model, Vis-Lens, combines a variational autoencoder and a diffusion model to generate realistic preferred images by directly modifying activation-regularized latent codes, without per-image iterative optimization. The framework is tested on artificial neural networks and on human visual cortex using fMRI data. It improves activation modulation and image realism compared with a recent state-of-the-art method.

entry.title: DynaSolver: A Neural Operator for Predicting Unsteady Flows Around Moving Boundaries
entry.summary: DynaSolver: A Neural Operator for Autoregressive 4D Flow Prediction with Dynamic Boundaries arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents DynaSolver, a neural operator that serves as a fast surrogate for computational fluid dynamics when boundaries move continuously. It also introduces RoboCFD-4D, a temporally resolved benchmark of robotic CFD cases with diverse morphologies and flow conditions. In experiments on this benchmark, DynaSolver achieves the best full-rollout accuracy among the learned CFD surrogates tested, and its advantage grows as the rollout proceeds.

entry.title: Checking how well time series foundation models express forecast uncertainty
entry.summary: Evaluating Uncertainty Calibration in Probabilistic Time Series Foundation Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines whether the uncertainty estimates from probabilistic time series foundation models are reliable. It proposes a taxonomy of how these models represent predictive uncertainty and a fine-grained framework for assessing calibration across multiple forecast horizons. Experiments on popular models find systematic miscalibration patterns that standard metrics often obscure, and the paper analyzes post-hoc recalibration methods.

entry.title: Scaling Theory for Multi-Epoch Pretraining: Late-Stage Overfitting and Ensembling
entry.summary: A Scaling Theory of Multi-Epoch Pretraining: Late-Time Overfitting and Ensembling arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how the number of training epochs and ensemble size jointly affect generalization when training data is fixed. In language model experiments on FineWeb, averaging logits reduces late-training performance decline and delays the optimal stopping point. The authors derive a dynamical mean-field theory for multi-epoch stochastic gradient descent in power-law random-feature ensembles and use it to give compute-allocation laws at fixed data and individual model size. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors derive a DMFT theory for multi-epoch SGD with ensembling and compute-allocation laws, reporting FineWeb language-model experiments where ensembles outperform wider or deeper single models.

entry.title: 3D-BBDA: Gradient-free black-box adaptation for robust 3D point cloud recognition
entry.summary: 3D-BBDA: Backpropagation-Free Black-Box Domain Adaptation for Robust 3D Point Cloud Recognition arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents 3D-BBDA, a framework that adapts a 3D point-cloud classifier to unlabeled target data using only the black-box outputs of a source-trained model, without access to source data or its parameters. It uses pseudo-label guided prototype alignment, a weighted module that fuses source and alignment logits, and Gaussian-perturbed prototypes as a fallback for missing class prototypes. The authors report improvements over baselines on four corrupted 3D benchmarks, and the method needs only a single forward pass with no gradient updates.

entry.title: FedReady: Bounded AI Agents for Preparing Federated Learning Sites
entry.summary: FedReady: Bounded Agents for Federation Formation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents FedReady, a system that uses bounded large language model agents to form a federation before federated learning begins, selecting task-eligible sites and preparing their local data and task code. The runtime manages workflow state and accepts agent-proposed artifacts only after checks tied to their digests. In experiments on 39 simulated retinal sites and four tasks, candidate discovery reached recall 1.00, and local eligibility verification removed all 17 false positives without losing any eligible site-task pair.

entry.title: Sonar-MoE: Updating Expert Weights During Backpropagation to Reduce Memory Use in Mixture-of-Experts Training
entry.summary: Sonar-MoE: In-Backward Expert Updates for Memory-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Training arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Sonar-MoE updates each expert tensor of a Mixture-of-Experts model during the backward pass and frees its gradient immediately, so the GPU holds at most one layer of expert gradients. Fine-tuning OLMoE-1B-7B and Granite-3.1-3B-A800M in bf16 lowered peak memory by 19% to 22%. Without expert gradient clipping, its updates are bitwise identical to standard training, and each step took 17% to 23% less time than standard training with global-norm clipping.

entry.title: NitiBench+: A Time-Aware Thai Legal Question Answering Benchmark Across 17 Domains
entry.summary: NitiBench+: A Temporal Thai Legal Question Answering Benchmark Across 17 Domains arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces NitiBench+, a Thai legal question answering benchmark with 1,670 items across 17 domains, built from decisions of three courts. For each cited section it provides both the text in force on the decision date and the current text.
