Evaluating 13 open-weight models, the authors find that using the current text of amended law or missing repealed law lowers scores, while a public leaderboard of 26 models shows that today's models still leave a wide gap on Thai law. ★★★★ Notable: The authors evaluate Thai legal QA on text in force at decision date, reporting score drops across 1,670 items and 13 open models.

entry.title: VeriHarm-Bench: Verifiably Measuring Harmful Success in Coding Agents
entry.summary: VeriHarm-Bench: Measuring Harmful Success in LLM Coding Agents Verifiably arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines "harmful success," where AI coding agents complete a benign task while also causing unintended harm, such as deleting unrelated files or weakening access controls. The authors introduce VeriHarm, a framework that automatically builds programmatically verifiable benchmarks to measure both task accuracy and harmful outcomes. Tests on frontier agents show about 95% task accuracy but only about 37% safe success rate, suggesting task-success metrics alone understate safety risks.

entry.title: BISECT: A low-rank method for continual learning with two-part spectral decomposition
entry.summary: BISECT: Bilevel Spectral Decomposition for Low-Rank Continual Learning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses exemplar-free continual learning on pre-trained Vision Transformers using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). It proposes BISECT, which splits a fixed rank budget into two orthogonal blocks: an invariant carrier built from dominant modes of the joint historical and current Gram matrix, and a novelty complement obtained by generalized Rayleigh whitening and orthogonal complement projection. After training, both blocks are folded back into the frozen backbone via a closed-form precision gate. The authors report that BISECT outperforms prompt, adapter, and LoRA baselines across eight incremental settings on five datasets, with no extra inference parameters or FLOPs.

entry.title: PlantVLM-Edge: Quantized Vision-Language Models for On-Device Crop Health Diagnosis
entry.summary: PlantVLM-Edge: Quantized Vision-Language Models for On-Device Crop Health Diagnosis arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents PlantVLM-Edge, a quantized vision-language framework that runs entirely on resource-constrained edge devices for conversational crop health diagnosis. It combines agricultural domain adaptation, post-training quantization, and an offline chat interface so growers can receive diagnoses, symptom explanations, and management guidance without cloud connectivity. Tested on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin with two VLMs and two diagnostic domains, 4-bit AWQ retains 98.6% of full-precision answer quality. The most compact form requires 2.01 GiB of weight memory and completes a 64-token diagnostic response in 0.78 seconds.

entry.title: Deep learning estimates how event rates depend on covariates in Poisson processes.
entry.summary: Nonparametric Intensity Estimation for Covariate-Driven Poisson Processes Using Deep Learning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies nonparametric maximum likelihood estimation of Poisson process intensities that depend on observed covariates, without assuming the intensity is bounded away from zero. It derives an oracle inequality for the covariate-averaged Hellinger distance and uses it to establish convergence rates for deep neural network-based estimators. Simulations and an analysis of Allen Brain Observatory neural spiking data compare these estimators with kernel methods.

entry.title: Can LLM Agents Work as Forward-Deployed Engineers? Requirement Discovery and Delivery for Enterprise Text-to-SQL
entry.summary: Can LLM Agents Be Forward-Deployed Engineers? Requirement Discovery and Delivery for Enterprise Text-to-SQL arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines whether LLM coding agents can act as forward-deployed engineers who uncover customer requirements and turn them into deployment decisions. Using a real enterprise text-to-SQL engagement, a simulated customer gives an ambiguous request, and the agent must identify acceptance criteria, data permissions, and hardware constraints before planning and running a post-training recipe. The strongest of 15 models discovered over 80% of withheld requirements, but only 25% of runs across eight coding-agent configurations passed all acceptance criteria in the delivery phase.

entry.title: Can AI Agents Improve Approximate Parameterizations in Earth System Climate Models?
entry.summary: Can LLM Agents Improve Imperfect Earth System Model Parameterizations? arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper tests whether large language model agents can help improve the parameterizations used in Earth system models, which approximate processes such as convection and cloud microphysics. Using warm-rain collision-coalescence as a test case, the agents synthesize literature, reimplement published schemes, and propose new functional forms as differentiable JAX code. Their outputs are compared with conventional schemes, data-driven emulators, and high-fidelity superdroplet simulations across ten language models. With expert guidance or iterative feedback, agents produced executable, mass-conserving code, though unattended performance varied by scheme and model.

entry.title: Variational Functional Neural Networks: Finding system states by optimizing integral physical functionals
entry.summary: Variational Functional Neural Networks (vfNN) arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes the variational functional neural network (vfNN), which finds system states by optimizing integral-form physical functionals such as the Lagrangian, Hamiltonian, or free energy. This avoids solving the Euler-Lagrange differential equations directly. Unlike physics-informed neural networks, it evaluates only lower-order derivatives and replaces ad hoc weights with physical scales. The authors report accurate results on benchmark systems governed by linear or nonlinear ordinary differential equations.

entry.title: An AI framework that automates power system studies and grid connection checks.
entry.summary: An Agentic Framework for Automated Power System Studies and Grid Connection Assessment arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents Grid Agents, combining the Grid Ontology, a searchable store of regulation, standards and engineering knowledge that evolves with use and whose answers cite evidence, with Grid Studio, a power-system engineering agent that relies on established solvers for its numbers. The authors compile eight benchmark families into 519 tasks and verify agents' work by replaying their tool calls. Grid Studio scores highest on these tasks, and with an optimiser in the loop its reinforcement packages cost 33-67% less on average than those designed by the agent alone.

entry.title: CoLa3D: Composable Latent 3D Scene Decomposition
entry.summary: CoLa3D: Composable Latent 3D Decomposition arXiv · Nov 3, 2026CoLa3D is a model that takes a single whole-scene latent, derived from one image or an existing scene mesh, and outputs a set of object meshes with consistent spatial layout that can be reassembled into a coherent scene. It uses a lightweight, query-based transformer that accepts 2D masks, 3D points, or learnable queries. On synthetic and real-world datasets it reports state-of-the-art performance on composable 3D scene decomposition, running 2 times faster than SAM 3D with less than 1% of its training data. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report decomposing objects directly within a shared scene latent, beating SAM 3D on synthetic and real data while running twice as fast.

entry.title: Adapting Skin Cancer Diagnosis Models Across Clinics Without Source Data
entry.summary: Contrastive Adapter Training and Consensus Knowledge Distillation for Multi-Source-Free Domain Adaptation in Skin Cancer Diagnosis arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes CAT-CKD, a method for adapting skin lesion classifiers from several labeled clinical sources to an unlabeled target dataset without access to the source data. It trains lightweight adapters in a frozen ViT backbone with supervised contrastive learning, then distills a consensus signal from multiple source models into a student model via KL divergence. The authors report an average AUROC of 86.1% across five public skin lesion datasets using 4.3M trainable parameters.

entry.title: Library of Layers (LoL): Runtime Reordering of Transformer Layers
entry.summary: Library of Layers (LoL): Adaptively Ordering Transformer Layers at Runtime arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces Library of Layers (LoL), a language model architecture that dynamically chooses and orders its transformer blocks from a global library during inference. A single hyperparameter, the library size, moves the model between parameter reuse and sparsity, unifying dense, depth-recurrent, and mixture-of-experts designs. Experiments cover text pretraining, synthetic sudoku and maze tasks, multilingual text, and safety data, where the layer orderings vary by task, language, and safe versus unsafe content.

entry.title: Grading Unlabeled Skills: Lessons from the WorkRB Skill Extraction Challenge at RecSys-HR 2026
entry.summary: Grading the Unannotated: Insights from the WorkRB Skill Extraction Challenge at RecSys-HR 2026 arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper reports on the WorkRB Skill Extraction Challenge at RecSys-HR 2026, which replaces binary scoring with graded relevance from 0 to 4 for each candidate skill, evaluated with nDCG@100. It describes the annotation method, five benchmark datasets, validation of an LLM judging cascade, and results from submitted systems. The authors find that top systems mainly gain by removing nonsensical candidates from the ranking window, and that these systems use several hundred times more parameters than the baselines they beat, leaving efficiency as the next challenge.

entry.title: DistDebug-Bench: Can LLM Agents Diagnose Bugs in Distributed Systems?
entry.summary: DistDebug-Bench: Can LLM Agents Diagnose Bugs in Distributed Systems? arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces DistDebug-Bench, a benchmark for testing whether LLM agents can diagnose code-level failures in complex distributed systems. It includes 120 real-world bugs from 11 widely used systems, covering 5 programming languages and 10 failure patterns. Evaluation of current LLMs and agents reveals substantial gaps with real debugging tasks, including tunnel vision from lacking explicit reasoning structure and nondeterminism from inconsistent tool-use scope.

entry.title: PanoTac: A Dense Three-Axis Tactile Sensor for Touch-Centric Robot Manipulation
entry.summary: PanoTac: A Dense Three-Axis Tactile Sensor for Robust Touch-Centric Manipulation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026PanoTac is a low-cost, compliant tactile fingertip that provides dense three-axis sensing, with normal and two shear response components at each sensing point. It operates at 60 Hz and costs under $50 per fingertip. Integrated into a visuo-tactile robotic system, it outperformed vision-only baselines by an average of 46.7 percentage points across test-tube preparation, grain scooping, and salt pouring. Ablations show that removing spatial contact information or shear feedback reduces performance.

entry.title: VIAS: A Method That Steers Language Models Toward Multiple Organisational Values Without Retraining
entry.summary: VIAS: Value-Isolating Activation Steering for Multi-Value Alignment and Compliance for Organisations arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines whether activation steering, which adds vectors to a language model's internal activations during generation without changing its weights, can improve organisational compliance beyond prompting alone. The authors propose Value-Isolating Activation Steering (VIAS), which builds steering vectors by contrasting responses to prompts that omit a single target value, reducing overlap between vectors for different values. Evaluated on the PROTECT workplace compliance dataset, VIAS combined with prompting satisfies every tagged value in 69.6% of scenarios for Qwen2.5-7B, 75.2% for Mistral-7B, and 72.6% for Phi-3.5-mini, outperforming prompting alone for all three models.

entry.title: Ask, Don't Equip: Question-Driven Coding Agents for Deep GPU Kernel Optimization
entry.summary: Ask, Don't Equip: Question-Driven Coding Agents for Deep Kernel Optimization arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents KernelSeek, a question-driven coding agent that speeds up an existing CUDA kernel on GPUs without operator-specific knowledge or a faster implementation to imitate. The authors report that on the same task, hardware, and evaluator, a tool-rich autonomous agent plateaued at 0.50x FlashAttention-3, while KernelSeek reached 1.13x. KernelSeek also produced dependency-free FlashAttention forward kernels for Hopper and Blackwell, with geometric-mean speedups of 1.16x over FlashAttention-3 and 1.46x over FlashAttention-4. The kernels, harness, question bank, and all traces are released.

entry.title: RASP: A Continual Learning Method That Reads All and Updates Sparsely in a Fixed-Size LoRA
entry.summary: RASP: Read-All, Sparse-Plasticity Continual Learning in a Stationary-Size LoRA arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes RASP, a parameter-efficient continual learning method for pre-trained Vision Transformers. It uses a single fixed-size LoRA adapter, reading all rank-1 components at inference while routing gradients to only a sparse subset of channels during training. A geometric consolidation index is used to attenuate updates and anchor important parameters to limit forgetting. The authors report that RASP matches or exceeds branch-expanding LoRA methods on CIFAR-100, CUB-200, ImageNet-R, and ImageNet-A under a constant parameter count.

entry.title: ST-GFM: A Spectral-Temporal Graph Forecaster with Provable Perturbation Bounds
entry.summary: ST-GFM: Spectral-Temporal Graph Forecasting with Measured Perturbation Bounds and Masked Spectral Reconstruction arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces ST-GFM, a graph forecasting model for sensor networks that filters inputs with Chebyshev and bidirectional diffusion filters and applies per-node temporal attention. It proves Frobenius-norm perturbation bounds for changes in the graph operator and evaluates the bounds on METR-LA and PEMS-BAY. A self-supervised Masked Spectral Reconstruction loss is active during the first 40 epochs and is reported to lower 60-minute MAE. ST-GFM is reported to outperform a retrained STAEformer baseline on both datasets.

entry.title: A matrix engine that serves both signal processing and neural network inference
entry.summary: A Cross-Domain Matrix Engine for Signal Processing and Deep Neural Net Inference arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes a single reconfigurable matrix engine that normally works as a systolic array and can switch, per operation, into a tensor-style engine with low-cost reconfiguration. This targets both low-latency small kernels in PHY signal processing and high-throughput large matrix multiplications in DNN inference. Simulations show up to 7.5x lower latency for small PHY kernels and up to 1.65x speedup on DNN workloads over a vanilla systolic array. Synthesis estimates the reconfigurable fabric adds only 8% power and 13.6% area overhead.

entry.title: Can AI do formal demography? A proof that vaccinating the oldest saves the most lives and years of life
entry.summary: Can AI Do Formal Demography? Why Vaccinating the Oldest Saves Both the Most Lives and the Most Years of Life arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper reports an experiment in which the AI model Claude was asked to explain and simplify a proof of a prior result: vaccinating the oldest against COVID-19 saves the most lives and years of life. The model proposed a shorter, more intuitive, and somewhat more general proof based on a known life-table identity and convexity. It states the condition for the result as convexity of the reciprocal of the hazard, and also gives an exact form of that condition.

entry.title: OLGA: label-free online gradient matching for keeping language models updated as data changes
entry.summary: Online Label-Free Gradient Matching for Continual Language Model Training arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces OLGA, a method for continually updating language models as their data shifts. It draws gradient matching targets from the model's own next-token predictions, so it needs no labels, and it keeps a running memory of synthetic examples for online data streams. The authors report a 10-point accuracy gain over the strongest selection baseline on five text classification benchmarks using as few as five examples.

entry.title: From Technical to Organizational Difficulty in AI Benchmarking
entry.summary: Harder Than the Task: From Technical to Organizational Difficulty in AI Benchmarking arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper argues that most AI benchmarks treat single technical tasks as the unit of evaluation, while real economically valuable work happens inside organizations, where tasks involve interdependent activities, distributed knowledge, authority, and conflicting interests. Drawing on organization theory, the authors develop a taxonomy of work structure and apply it to existing benchmarks. They find that few prominent benchmarks cover organizational dimensions. The authors conclude that AI benchmarks should increasingly assess agents' ability to navigate organizational conditions.

entry.title: Hybrid Framework Predicting Nebraska Lake Visitors Using Interpretable Time Features and Anomaly Filtering
entry.summary: A Hybrid Visitor Prediction Framework using Interpretable Temporal features, Integrating IQR and Anomaly Detection in Lakes in Nebraska arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper predicts daily visitor numbers at Nebraska lakes using spatial, basic temporal, and interpretable temporal features. It compares several base models and hybrid ensembles, and studies the effect of lag features and two outlier handling methods, IQR and anomaly detection. Removing anomalies reduced error metrics, and anomaly detection outperformed IQR. In the reported cross-validation, the voting ensemble performed better than the compared base models.

entry.title: Identifying a shear piezoelectric coefficient with neural networks that enforce exact boundary and initial conditions
entry.summary: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents a constrained physics-informed neural network that builds boundary and initial conditions directly into its output, so they hold exactly without penalty terms. On simulated data, it recovers the shear piezoelectric coefficient e15 non-destructively from sparse, noisy subsurface wavefield observations. In comparison with a soft-penalty baseline, the constrained formulations achieve mean e15 errors between 0.15% and 0.51%.

entry.title: Tilted Convexity and an Exact Offline-Online Separation
entry.summary: Tilted Convexity and an Exact Offline-Online Separation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper weakens the three equivalent descriptions of convexity with one distortion parameter γ in (0,1], producing nested function classes that are convex at γ=1. The authors show these classes have convex effective domains, with local minimizers that are global and local Lipschitz continuity on the relative interior. Assuming NP≠RP, no polynomial-time randomized algorithm achieves sublinear α-regret online for fixed γ in (0,1), so γ is the exact online coefficient while the offline coefficient is one. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a distortion parameter γ weakening convexity, prove nested classes, and report an exact offline-online separation with a hardness lower bound.

entry.title: A Bayesian method for safely controlling unknown systems using only input-output data
entry.summary: A Bayesian Framework for Safe Optimal Control of Unknown Systems from Input-Output Data arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes a Bayesian framework that learns a nonlinear, stochastic system from input-output data using particle Markov chain Monte Carlo, capturing joint uncertainty over dynamics and latent states. It provides a validation procedure with probabilistic guarantees of constraint satisfaction under arbitrary causal control laws. The control design penalizes the conditional value-at-risk of the constraint function and adapts a calibration to balance performance and robustness. The framework is extended to receding-horizon control and demonstrated on optimal control of a vertical farm.

entry.title: HIVE-Diff: High-Frame-Rate HDR Video Reconstruction from One LDR Frame and Events
entry.summary: HIVE-Diff: High Frame Rate HDR Video Reconstruction from a Single LDR Frame and Events arXiv · Nov 3, 2026HIVE-Diff reconstructs multiple high dynamic range (HDR) video frames from a single low dynamic range (LDR) reference frame and event camera data. It uses an event-conditioned video diffusion framework that splits the task into event-guided temporal generation and HDR content completion. Because paired real HDR-event data is scarce, the model is trained on synthetic data and adapted to real event domains using LDR-event sequences as proxy supervision with teacher-student distillation. The authors report strong reconstruction quality on synthetic and multiple real-world datasets.

entry.title: Unrolled gradients in disguise: linking interpolation and Jacobian regularization for stable neural dynamics.
entry.summary: Unrolled gradients in disguise: bridging interpolation-based and Jacobian regularization for stable neural dynamics arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Hybrid models and neural differential equations often become unstable or inaccurate during long-term integration. The paper shows that two common stabilization methods, training on interpolated or noisy samples and regularizing the Jacobian of the learned representation, both approximate the gradients obtained from unrolled learning. Building on this view, the authors derive a principled and complete regularization approach for training and demonstrate its effect on the stability of learned dynamical systems.

entry.title: Tracking class probabilities during discrete diffusion for interpretable, controllable text and sequence generation
entry.summary: Online Class Posteriors for Interpretable and Controllable Discrete Diffusion arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes a theoretical framework that tracks class-conditional posteriors online in discrete diffusion models by combining conditional and unconditional predictions. In masked language modeling, tokens matching a class raise the posterior while contradictory tokens lower it. The authors also show the posterior supports logical guidance operations (AND, OR, NOT) for controlling generation, and discuss a difference in classifier-free guidance between discrete and continuous settings.

entry.title: Improving Hamiltonian learning via local energy decomposition
entry.summary: Improving Hamiltonian Learning through Local Energy Decomposition arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces the Local Multiscale Hamiltonian Neural Network (LM-HNN), which splits the energy into kinetic and potential parts and represents each as a sum of shared local functions over multiple interaction neighborhoods. The authors state that this makes fine-scale energy structure easier to learn while preserving Hamiltonian dynamics. Experiments on low-dimensional, interacting, and fast-slow systems report more accurate Hamiltonian derivatives and long-horizon rollouts than competing structure-preserving models, along with better generalization to unseen energy levels.

entry.title: Intent2CAD: How Semantic-Parametric Supervision Shapes Text-to-CAD Generation
entry.summary: Intent2CAD: How Semantic-Parametric Supervision Shapes Text-to-CAD Generation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how to make text-to-CAD generation produce programs with reusable design intent, expressed as semantic features, parameters, and parametric relations. The authors build IntentCAD-100K, a 100K text-code dataset converted into executable CadQuery programs, and IntentCAD-Edit-1K for zero-shot editing. Their two-stage lifting pipeline shows that semantic lifting improves generation reliability and feature recovery, while parametric lifting makes relation structure explicit and improves relation-aware editing.

entry.title: Error buildup in repeated second-order machine unlearning
entry.summary: Error Accumulation in Second-Order Sequential Machine Unlearning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how approximation errors accumulate when training data are deleted one request after another in machine unlearning, in a high-dimensional regime where the parameter count is proportional to the sample size. It compares partial and perfect unlearning privacy settings and uses conjugate gradient to approximate inverse Hessian-vector products within Newton iterations. The theory shows that one to three Newton-CG updates, depending on the certification type, suffice for successful certification and vanishing population-risk degradation, and experiments report computational gains over gradient-based updates on ill-conditioned problems.

entry.title: Proximal sampling with fewer gradient queries for non-convex densities.
entry.summary: Subpolynomial-Query Proximal Sampling Beyond Log-Concavity arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies how many gradient queries are needed to sample from a density proportional to exp(-V), where V has a Lipschitz gradient but need not be convex. It uses a proximal sampler that alternates Gaussian perturbation with conditional sampling from noisy observations, implemented with a high-order noisy conditional sampler. Under a log-Sobolev inequality and under a Poincaré inequality, the authors give query complexity guarantees, and an oracle lower bound shows a stationary point is insufficient under the Poincaré inequality.

entry.title: Playing Dumb: How a Chess Transformer Simulates Users at Different Skill Levels
entry.summary: Playing Dumb: How a Chess Transformer Simulates Users Across Skill Levels arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies Maia-2, a chess transformer that predicts human moves based on player skill. Using probes, the authors show that its internal encoding of 172 chess concepts stays nearly constant across skill levels. Fine-tuning only the final output layer raised best-move accuracy in the lowest skill band from 14.4% to 82.8%. The results suggest weaker play reflects how retained knowledge is used rather than a lack of knowledge. ★★★★ Notable: The authors separate knowledge encoding from knowledge use in Maia-2, reporting probes, output-layer fine-tuning, and sparse autoencoder steering, with lowest-skill best-move accuracy rising from 14.4

entry.title: One-time alignment to make foundation vision models interpretable at scale
entry.summary: Align Once to Explain: Feature Alignment for Scalable B-cosification of Foundational Vision Transformers arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents ALOE, a one-time, label-free feature alignment method that converts foundational vision models into inherently interpretable B-cos variants. The aligned B-cos backbone can serve as a drop-in replacement across several downstream tasks. The method works across supervised, self-supervised, and vision-language pre-training, and it outperforms vanilla B-cosification on classification while remaining competitive with foundation backbones in transfer tasks.

entry.title: Linking neural tangent kernel theory to reinforcement learning for deep function approximation
entry.summary: Bridging Neural Tangent Kernel Analysis and Reinforcement Learning for Deep Function Approximation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper extends neural tangent kernel (NTK) theory to reinforcement learning by introducing a temporal-difference (TD) flow formulation that handles time-varying mini-batches and TD targets. It derives a closed-form solution for how the value function evolves in an overparametrized setting. The authors also propose an optimization-based state-space exploration method that uses this solution together with environment constraints to model feasible states. Experiments on a deterministic grid environment show efficient learning, adaptation to shifts in the training data distribution, and improved sample efficiency from the exploration strategy.

entry.title: A continuously updated leaderboard for graph machine learning results
entry.summary: A Living Leaderboard for Graph Machine Learning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces a living leaderboard for graph learning that organizes reported results by dataset so new results can be compared with prior ones. As of 15 October 2026, the authors' LLM-based extraction pipeline gathered 27,723 eligible results across 111 datasets from 885 peer-reviewed papers. The analysis finds that legacy datasets are still widely used and that many result tables report baseline numbers far below those already in the literature.

entry.title: Testing whether depth-based geometry improves lunar terrain traversability estimation across datasets
entry.summary: Evaluating Depth-Augmented Visual Features for Cross-Dataset Lunar Traversability Estimation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines whether adding depth, surface normal, and combined geometric information to visual features improves lunar traversability estimation. The authors train a weakly supervised model on sparse pairwise annotations and evaluate it in in-domain and cross-domain settings using two terrestrial analogue datasets and the real Chang'E PCAM lunar dataset. Simple geometric augmentation gave no consistent gain over a strong visual-only baseline. The choice of training source was the dominant factor in transfer quality to real lunar imagery.

entry.title: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share Human Researchers' Research Taste?
entry.summary: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share the Research Taste of Human Researchers? arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces IdeaTaste, a benchmark that scores language models by how closely the research proposals they write, based on a literature snapshot from 2025, match papers that the same communities published in 2026. Experiments cover six models and four research areas, with over 90,000 proposals. The models reach about 26% of human level on citation matching and only 18% on idea matching, mainly lacking concrete approaches and research plans.

entry.title: Two-stage open-set recognition that avoids magnitude collapse
entry.summary: Circumventing Magnitude Collapse via Modular Two-Stage Open-Set Recognition arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper treats open-set recognition as a two-stage pipeline of representation learning followed by postprocessing, and systematically studies how the two interact across dataset scales and with or without known unknown data. It identifies a failure mode called magnitude collapse, where representation methods using known unknown data degrade at large scale and irreversibly destroy discriminative information. Combining a simple K+1 class classifier baseline with magnitude-aware postprocessing achieves state-of-the-art results while avoiding this collapse, and the authors argue that small-scale evaluations do not predict large-scale performance.

entry.title: Temporal Island Sparse Autoencoders for Interpreting Clinical Time-Series Models
entry.summary: Temporal Island Sparse Autoencoders for Interpreting Clinical Time-Series Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces the Temporal Island Sparse Autoencoder (TI-SAE), which learns a patient-shared clinical concept dictionary from a frozen predictive model's representations. Each dictionary entry combines learned temporal Gaussian islands showing when a concept is active with a sparse vector indicating which variables are involved. TI-SAE was evaluated across five backbone architectures on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, producing structured clinical concepts and performing well on standard faithfulness benchmarks.

entry.title: Controlling POMDPs with Limited Memory: Fundamental Limits and an Efficient Design Method
entry.summary: Finite-Memory Control of POMDPs: Fundamental Limits and Efficient Design arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how a finite-memory controller can control partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) near optimally, since exact belief tracking is generally impossible with finite memory. The authors derive an information-theoretic converse giving a fundamental lower bound on the loss of any finite-memory controller, and introduce the notion of a decision witness for belief states whose confusion causes unavoidable loss. They propose RECAP, a constructive quantization method for designing representative memory states, and prove an upper bound on the optimality gap of any RECAP codebook. Experiments on 11 POMDP benchmarks show RECAP outperforms finite-memory representation baselines under the same memory budget.

entry.title: DeliverBench: Testing whether AI agents can deliver full multi-stage professional projects
entry.summary: DeliverBench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Delivering Realistic Multi-Stage Professional Projects arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces DeliverBench, a benchmark that tests whether AI agents can take a professional project from initial brief to final delivery. It contains 11 projects in areas such as financial due diligence, legal contract drafting, and drug safety reporting, built by 13 domain experts from real materials and divided into 150 subtasks with 2 to 15 rounds of new materials and client feedback. Agents inherit their own earlier errors, and experts score each checkpoint and the final package. The best of seven model-harness systems scored 65.0 out of 100 on final delivery and passed 50.0% of subtasks at a 90-point threshold. The authors conclude that task-level ability does not simply add up to successful delivery, which also requires keeping the work coherent as it evolves. ★★★★ Notable: The authors evaluate multi-stage professional project delivery with expert rubrics, reporting the best system scores 65.0 out of 100 on final delivery.

entry.title: Low-rank Clebsch-Gordan coupling for rotation-equivariant spherical weather forecasting
entry.summary: Low-Rank Clebsch--Gordan Coupling for Equivariant Spherical Forecasting arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces LCG-SFNO, a spherical forecasting model that adds low-rank Clebsch-Gordan tensor product interactions while preserving SO(3) rotational equivariance throughout the learned operator. It also presents SSHCG, a sparse GPU implementation that makes this coupling practical at forecasting scale. On shallow-water dynamics and the ERA5-based WeatherBench benchmark, the model reduces rotational error to numerical precision and improves forecast skill over SFNO on WeatherBench.

entry.title: Agentic AI orchestration for Open RAN resilience during signaling storms
entry.summary: From Reactive to Agentic Resilience: Multi-Timescale AI-RAN Orchestration Under Signaling Storms arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines how Open RAN and AI-RAN networks can stay resilient when mass device attachments create signaling storms. It proposes a three-tier framework in which a service-level orchestrator sets policy, per-site agents anticipate storms, and a deterministic near-real-time loop enforces decisions, tested with a discrete-event attach simulator. The agentic controller, by reading a scheduled event from a calendar and provisioning ahead of it, approaches the resilience of a fully provisioned server pool at a quarter of its capacity.

entry.title: VidDub: Two-Step Video Dubbing via Replacement-Aware Distillation
entry.summary: VidDub: Replacement-Aware Distillation for Two-Step Video Dubbing arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents VidDub, a video dubbing method that synthesizes lip movements matching new speech while keeping the speaker's identity, head pose, and background. Its replacement-aware training masks source-mouth reconstruction losses on replacement-audio samples, supervising the mouth only through audio-visual synchronization. The full diffusion editor is distilled into a two-step denoising model. Across four benchmarks, the final model reports strong lip synchronization, visual quality, identity preservation, and visual speech recognition.

entry.title: Depth image upsampling guided by anisotropic total generalized variation
entry.summary: Image Guided Depth Upsampling using Anisotropic Total Generalized Variation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents a new method for upsampling depth images from cameras such as Kinect, whose lateral resolution is limited. It uses an anisotropic diffusion tensor computed from a high-resolution intensity image to guide a convex optimization with higher-order regularization. The primal-dual algorithm is parallelized and runs at multiple frames per second. The authors report better speed and accuracy than existing methods on the Middlebury 2007 datasets and introduce new datasets with highly accurate ground truth based on real sensor data.

entry.title: TaoMate-HD: Progressive-Resolution Autoregressive Audio-Video Generation
entry.summary: TaoMate-HD: Progressive-Resolution Autoregressive Audio-Video Generation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026TaoMate-HD is an autoregressive model for generating high-resolution audio and video in streaming form, aimed at digital humans that keep speaking as new text arrives. Each short chunk first gets two low-resolution denoising steps for coarse video structure, then a final step refines it to high resolution, with audio generated along the same process. The model keeps audiovisual history across chunks and text updates, and reports a 1.6x speedup over direct high-resolution generation, a further 1.9x from stage-parallel deployment, and an 11.18 percentage point reduction in character error rate from continuation training.

entry.title: TaoMate-FVSR: Audio-Guided Facial Video Restoration
entry.summary: TaoMate-FVSR:Audio-Guided Facial Video Restoration arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents a framework for restoring faces in AI-generated videos, where small facial regions such as lips and teeth are often poorly rendered. The method uses audio guidance within a reference-guided video flow model, combining source-noise mixing with structured reference injection. On talking-head restoration benchmarks, it achieves the best paired perceptual similarity and synchronization scores among the compared methods.

entry.title: Progressive multi-scale super-resolution with cascaded bicubic anchors and mutual refinement
entry.summary: Progressive Multi-Scale Super-Resolution via Cascaded Bicubic Anchors and Inter-Scale Mutual Refinement arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces PMS-SR, a progressive network that takes one low-resolution input and produces x2, x4, and x8 super-resolved outputs in a single forward pass, using a Transformer backbone. Each scale is predicted as a residual over the bicubic upsampling of the previous scale, and a second stage lets the scales refine one another through feedback, deformable alignment, and fusion. Trained on DF2K, the 7.95M-parameter model reports higher PSNR than all compared multi-scale methods at x4 and x8 on five standard benchmarks.

entry.title: CrowdForge: How Audio and Visual Audience Participation Affects Agency, Collaboration, and Engagement in AI-Mediated MR Concerts
entry.summary: CrowdForge: Effects of Audio and Visual Audience Participation Modalities on Agency, Collaboration, and Engagement in AI-Mediated MR Performances arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents CrowdForge, a system where audiences collectively control AI-generated music and mixed reality virtual environments during a live performance by a guitarist and DJ. A mixed-methods concert study compared audio, visual, and combined audio-visual interaction conditions. The authors found that observability is the main driver of audience agency, with visual interaction giving easily seen feedback and audio parameters offering macro-level control over the music.

entry.title: LAND: Adaptively choosing how many samples to draw for best-of-N selection
entry.summary: LAND: Learning an Adaptive Number of Draws for Bayesian Best-of-N Selection arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Best-of-N decoding improves text generation by sampling several candidates and keeping the best one, but it spends the same compute on every input. LAND learns from calibration data how score distributions vary across sources, updates its belief as scores come in, and stops sampling when another draw is expected to add too little value. In machine-translation experiments across several models and language pairs, LAND scored higher on MetricX than fixed best-of-N at equal average compute, and needed roughly 20-40% fewer candidates for the same translation quality.

entry.title: ASCoR: Asymmetric Semantic-Spatial Learning for Remote Sensing Domain Generalization
entry.summary: ASCoR: Asymmetric Semantic-Spatial Learning for Remote Sensing Domain Generalization arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses source-only domain generalization for remote sensing semantic segmentation, where models must predict reliably on unseen domains without target-domain data during training. The authors propose ASCoR, an asymmetric framework built on SAM3 that combines a text-conditioned semantic branch, a fixed-budget dynamic adaptive LoRA, and a separate dense spatial branch, integrated by a lightweight reliability router. Experiments on ISPRS, LoveDA, and OpenEarthMap across nine cross-domain transfers show a mean IoU of 68.61% on six ISPRS transfers, with best results on all three LoveDA/OpenEarthMap transfers.

entry.title: A neural-operator stand-in for LISFLOOD-FP that forecasts floods in Forlì, Italy
entry.summary: A Geometry-Informed Neural Operator surrogate of LISFLOOD-FP for rapid pluvial-fluvial flood forecasting: the case of Forlì, Italy arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The authors present a time-dependent geometry-informed neural operator (GINO) that serves as a fast surrogate for the physically based flood model LISFLOOD-FP, applied to Forlì, Italy, after the May 2023 Emilia-Romagna floods. It uses only river stage and rain gauge data and was tested on 38 observed events not seen during training, reaching a CSI of 0.934 at 0.05 m. A 72-hour forecast takes 1.7 s instead of 55 s, and a 50-member ensemble takes 6.2 s.

entry.title: RangeFinder: Predicting Ligand Property Ranges from Protein Pockets
entry.summary: RangeFinder: Predicting Ligand Property Ranges from Protein Pockets arXiv · Nov 3, 2026RangeFinder is an SE(3)-equivariant transformer model for protein pockets, trained and evaluated on BioLiP2 data. It predicts ranges over nine physicochemical ligand properties directly from pocket structure, chemistry, and evolutionary context. It achieves a range-IoU of 0.464 ± 0.002 at 12.2 ms per pocket, and is presented as a fast molecular filter that narrows the ligand search space before docking, generation, or synthesis.

entry.title: Mixed-methods study of social and technical factors driving adoption of crime-reporting apps in cities
entry.summary: Mixed-Methods Exploration of Sociotechnical Factors to Improve Adoption of Crime-Reporting Apps in Urban Communities arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This study used a mixed-methods approach to identify factors that encourage urban residents to adopt crime-reporting apps. It combined two focus groups, an analysis of 660 app reviews, and a survey of 505 urban residents analyzed with PLS-SEM. Initial perceived usefulness fades over time, while sustained use depends on perceived value, formed by safety, anonymity, autonomy, and camaraderie. Perceived value was the strongest predictor of behavioral intention, which in turn strongly predicted actual use.

entry.title: When language models take harmful actions to protect their goals
entry.summary: Characterizing When Language Models Take Harmful Actions to Protect Their Assigned Goals arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper treats agentic misalignment, such as blackmailing an executive to avoid replacement, and alignment faking, such as complying with harmful requests during training to keep values unchanged, as one shared decision structure. It formalizes this as a goal-harm conflict in which a model must either take a harmful action or refuse and lose its goal. The authors study this conflict under protocols from forced-choice prompts to simulated agentic environments, using both a logit view based on answer-token probabilities and a sampling view that classifies open-ended responses with an LM judge.

entry.title: EO-Jev: A Decision Model for Earth Observation
entry.summary: EO-Jev: Decision Model for Earth Observation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies decision models for Earth observation imagery, which output probabilities over candidate answers in a single forward pass. The authors diagnose d3-flash (8.4B parameters) across 30 settings from 23 public benchmarks. They then apply low-rank fine-tuning on public EO training splits to produce EO-Jev, which improves over d3-flash on 26 of 30 settings with a modest drop in general decision performance.

entry.title: Fusing Across Samples: Hypergraph Regularization for Multimodal Retrieval Representations
entry.summary: Fuse To Align: Multimodal Representation Learning for Retrieval via Hypergraph Regularization arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes a training-time hypergraph fusion framework that connects observed modalities within samples and across semantically related samples, so representation learning can use evidence beyond a single sample. The retrieval pipeline is unchanged at inference, and the hypergraph is discarded after training. Experiments on eleven zero-shot video-text and audio-text retrieval benchmarks report improvements over GRAM and HyperGRAM, including positive gains under missing-modality evaluation.

entry.title: Every Pixel Is an Option: A System One Model for Medical Ultrasound Biometry
entry.summary: Every Pixel Is an Option: A System One Model for Medical Ultrasound Biometry arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents Kev-Bio, a vision-language model that uses clinical measurement questions to guide the detection of anatomical landmarks in ultrasound images. Inspired by System One decision models, it generates queries for each caliper endpoint from the language model's decision representations and matches them to shared dense ultrasound features to produce spatial probability maps. On the nine-view FU/GU Biometry 2026 dataset, Kev-Bio achieves a mean radial error of 22.50 pixels and a clinical measurement mean absolute error of 15.38, outperforming the compared baselines overall.

entry.title: Machine learning for multidimensional suicide risk assessment using EHR data
entry.summary: Multidimensional Suicide Risk Assessment with Machine Learning using Electronic Health Records arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents a machine learning framework that estimates suicide-related outcomes from MIMIC-IV electronic health records. It defines a composite outcome from codes for suicidal ideation, suicide attempts, prior suicidal behavior, and intentional self-harm, using age-matched resampling to handle class imbalance. After isotonic calibration, the XGBoost model performed best in the matched cohort. SHAP analysis indicates that diagnostic burden, depression-related features, age, personality-disorder history, violence-related social determinants, and medical comorbidity raise predicted probabilities.

entry.title: Neural actor-critic learning with minimax critics and reflected Langevin sampling
entry.summary: Neural Actor--Critic Learning with Minimax Critics and Reflected Langevin Sampling arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes a neural actor-critic method for improving continuous-action policies. The critic uses a regularized minimax Bellman estimator over sigmoid networks, while the actor samples actions with a finite reflected Langevin sampler driven by the fitted critic gradient. The authors derive finite-sample guarantees for value and action-gradient errors and propagate them to return guarantees, and compare performance against baselines on simulated control, logged continuous-control data, and a simulated decision task.

entry.title: Certifying graph neural networks against label and structure poisoning
entry.summary: Certifying Graph Neural Networks Against Label and Structure Poisoning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies certified robustness of graph-structured learning against poisoning attacks, where adversaries manipulate training data. It shows that existing partition-and-aggregation certification methods from images fail on graphs because of label and structure sparsity. The authors propose ST-GPA, a semi-supervised framework that adds pseudo-labels and synthetic edges to each graph partition. Across multiple benchmarks, it improves robustness guarantees against node-label and graph-structure poisoning while maintaining strong clean accuracy.

entry.title: NormMoX: A normative expert-mixture model that explains autism classification from structural and functional brain MRI.
entry.summary: NormMoX: A Normative Mixture of Experts for Explainable Autism Classification from Structural and Functional MRI arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents NormMoX, which uses normative models of healthy brains as a shared reference, learning each person's deviations from age- and sex-expected values for each brain measure. A neural expert per modality converts these deviations into evidence scores for autism, and a fusion head, MoX, compares them with typical controls before combining them. On 1,035 participants in ABIDE I, it reached an AUROC of 0.728 ± 0.004 in repeated cross-validation, above linear, single-modality and deep fusion baselines, and shows which modality each person deviates in.

entry.title: FLAMIA: Fast, causally safe low-precision attention kernels for NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs
entry.summary: FLAMIA: FLAsh MIcroscaling Attention for Fast and Causally Safe Training on Blackwell arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents FLAMIA, a family of attention kernels for NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs that support MXFP8 and mixed NVFP4/FP8 training. The design reuses quantized operands through token-block scaling, adds safeguards against scale-induced causal leakage, and keeps forward and backward computations consistent. On causal packed-document workloads, the MXFP8 path speeds up combined attention calls by roughly 1.06 to 1.42 times over the fastest baseline, and training stability and quality are validated on Llama-style pretraining.

entry.title: ArabGeoText: Vision-Language Models with Tools for Reading Arabic Map Labels
entry.summary: ArabGeoText: Tool-Augmented Vision-Language Models for Arabic Geospatial Text Spotting arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces ArabGeoText, a benchmark of Arabic geographic labels such as road and district names on maps of 970 locations in Riyadh and Jeddah, with each location shown in OpenStreetMap and remote sensing overlay views. The authors propose a framework combining YOLO26 localization and crop rectification with a Qwen3.5-4B recognizer adapted by LoRA. Experiments report that this framework outperforms direct LoRA-adapted Qwen3.5-4B spotting across both image views and test cities.

entry.title: SIMPLE Law: A Four-Parameter Model for Predicting LLM Inference Energy
entry.summary: The SIMPLE Law for Energy Cost of LLM Inference arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper derives closed-form expressions for the computation and memory-access costs of LLM inference from architectural hyperparameters and proposes SIMPLE, a four-parameter energy model that separates prefill from decode. Tested on 13 dense LLMs from six families on NVIDIA H100 GPUs, it reaches R² of 0.969 and 11.97% MAPE without per-model calibration. The paper also analyzes how input length, grouped-query attention, reasoning token budgets, and agentic serving with prefix caching affect energy use. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive closed-form energy models from architecture hyperparameters, proposing a four-parameter law reporting R2 0.969 and 11.97% MAPE across 13 LLMs, relevant to inference energy planning.

entry.title: From FAIR to AI-FAIR: Metadata-First Infrastructure for AI Science
entry.summary: From FAIR to AI-FAIR Metadata-First Infrastructure for AI-Enabled Science arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes AI-FAIR metadata criteria, an extension of the original FAIR data principles, placing AI-enabled science within a bidirectional Question-Data-Model triangle. It also introduces an agentic evaluation workflow that rates existing datasets against both AI-FAIR and traditional FAIR criteria and gives actionable feedback where critical metadata is missing or incomplete. The goal is to ensure that the scientists who generate data benefit from AI advances built on it, closing the model-data loop.

entry.title: Using multilingual sentiment lexicons to steer sentiment in low-resource languages
entry.summary: Steering with Multilingual Lexicons for Sentiment Control in Low-Resource Languages arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines whether multilingual sentiment lexicons can replace the sentence-level contrastive data normally needed for activation steering in languages where such data is scarce. Across three model families, aggregated multilingual lexicons outperform English-derived steering vectors for mid- and low-resource languages, while monolingual lexicons work better for languages the model specialized in during pre-training. The authors also give a mechanistic analysis of how representational density, pre-training priors, and vector magnitude affect cross-lingual steering.

entry.title: MultiInpaintCOCO: A Multilingual Benchmark for Fine-Grained Visual Understanding
entry.summary: MultiInpaintCOCO: Fine-Grained Visual Understanding in Multiple Languages arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper extends the English InpaintCOCO dataset, which focuses on fine-grained visual details, to 13 languages from five language families, producing MultiInpaintCOCO with 953 minimal-pair examples. The authors test several state-of-the-art multilingual multimodal retrieval models, including CLIP-like encoders and large language models. Results show performance drops substantially for lower-resource languages, and most models prefer English captions over correct non-English ones, with the degree of bias varying across architectures.

entry.title: LLMs rely on specialist tools to generalize to unseen MS/MS structure elucidation
entry.summary: LLMs Depend on Specialist Tools for Out-of-Distribution Generalization in MS/MS Structural Elucidation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper tests whether a frontier language model can propose molecular structures directly from tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) spectra without candidate lists or reference libraries. The authors built a 100-analyte benchmark from MassSpecGym, split into in-distribution compounds that are well documented in the literature and out-of-distribution compounds that are essentially undocumented. Without tools, the model reached 52% Top-1 accuracy in-distribution but only 2% out-of-distribution; access to de novo structure generators raised out-of-distribution accuracy to as much as 38%, and that agent outperformed the standalone de novo models.

entry.title: Calibrated Multiaccuracy: Sample Complexity of Deterministic and Randomized Predictors
entry.summary: Calibrated Multiaccuracy: Deterministic and Randomized Sample Complexity arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies calibrated multiaccuracy, where a predictor is globally calibrated and multiaccurate with respect to a bounded test family G, meaning its residuals are uncorrelated with every test function. The authors determine its sample complexity, which differs from that of multicalibration, and give an upper bound achieved by a randomized predictor. For deterministic predictors they establish a tight rate, revealing a genuine sample-complexity separation between the two. ★★★★ Notable: The authors establish tight sample complexity for calibrated multiaccuracy, separating it from multicalibration and showing a deterministic versus randomized predictor gap.

entry.title: An axiomatic framework for reinforcement learning in systems where only some agents can be controlled
entry.summary: An Axiomatic Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Open Multi-Agent Systems arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies reinforcement learning in open multi-agent systems, where only some agents are controllable, such as in smart grids. It derives value function learning from the Shapley axioms (Efficiency, Symmetry, and Linearity) within the n-agent ad hoc teamwork (NAHT) setting, linking it to cooperative game theory and the Shapley value for Dec-POMDPs. Two generic algorithmic templates, Shapley Machines and Banzhaf Machines, are introduced and can be combined with standard reinforcement learning methods. The authors report improved learning efficiency and generalisation to unseen agent types on NAHT benchmark tasks.

entry.title: SQLoom: Set-Contrastive Learning for Text-to-SQL Syntax, Semantics, and Logic
entry.summary: SQLoom: Set-Contrastive Learning of Syntactic, Semantic, and Logical Dependencies for Text-to-SQL arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents SQLoom, a constraint-aware fine-tuning method for large language models that converts natural language questions into SQL queries. It supervises outputs at three levels (syntactic validity, semantic alignment with the question, and logical consistency across clauses) using a set-contrastive objective that favors correct output sets over minimally different incorrect ones. On Spider, the approach raises Qwen3-1.7B's execution accuracy on the development set from 62.9% zero-shot to 88.7%, and reaches 73.4% on BIRD development.

entry.title: Learning rewards that transfer across environments by actively choosing which dynamics to study
entry.summary: Inferring Transferable Rewards via Active Inverse Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Inverse reinforcement learning seeks to recover expert rewards that remain useful when the environment's dynamics change. The paper proposes a two-phase method that first cycles through available dynamics to get a reliable reward estimate, then actively selects dynamics to reduce uncertainty about the expert reward. The authors provide sample complexity guarantees on transfer that hold for any dynamics, with a rate independent of the number of available dynamics. Experiments show the method substantially reduces the number of expert demonstrations needed to learn a transferable reward.

entry.title: ENGINE: A Zeroth-Order Method for Fine-Tuning Large Language Models
entry.summary: ENGINE: Endogenous Variational MultiScale Optimization for Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes ENGINE, a zeroth-order (ZO) method for memory-efficient fine-tuning of large language models. It alternates between a low-dimensional subspace and the full high-dimensional space, adapting variational multiscale theory from computational mechanics to dynamic optimization. On standard LLM benchmarks, the authors report higher accuracy and faster convergence than existing ZO methods, with up to a 2.61x speed-up in forward passes and no additional peak memory.

entry.title: Top-k Retrieval Leaves Memory Value Undetermined
entry.summary: Top-k Retrieval Leaves Memory Value Undetermined arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper asks which memory values an agent can infer from its retrieval log alone. It proves that under top-k retrieval, no memory value is determined however many episodes are logged. The proposed LEDGER method estimates only the determined Shapley values, with confidence intervals, and raises the fraction of determined memories on pooled HotpotQA from 0.001 to 0.797. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove top-k retrieval logs leave memory values undetermined and propose LEDGER, reporting a large rise in determined memories on HotpotQA.

entry.title: Mesh-agnostic refinement of 3D human body shape latent encodings
entry.summary: Mesh-Agnostic Refinement Models for Latent Space Encoding of 3D Human Body Shapes arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes a framework for refining reconstructions from parametric human body models such as SMPL. It uses the geometric difference between an initial decoded surface and a target mesh, without needing vertex correspondences. The framework has three methods: Latent-VaRefine corrects the latent code using varifold-distance gradients, Vertex-VaRefine predicts vertex displacements in a canonical pose with a DiffusionNet backbone, and ElaOpt optimizes surface deformation under elastic regularization and normal-direction constraints.

entry.title: ReVA-HPE: Relative 6DoF Head Pose Estimation Using Synthetic Training and Virtual Anchors
entry.summary: ReVA-HPE: Relative 6DoF Head Pose Estimation with Synthetic Pose Supervision and Personalized Virtual Anchors arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies head pose estimation from a single face image by estimating the relative geometric change between a query image and an anchor image, extended to full 6DoF with translation. It reconstructs a personalized avatar from one unlabeled enrollment image and renders virtual anchors with known poses, using multi-anchor consensus for rotation and the real enrollment image for translation. The estimator is trained only on synthetic face renderings. On real benchmarks, the authors report state-of-the-art rotation accuracy on BIWI and competitive metric translation.

entry.title: Specificity Bias and the Wikipedia Paradox: Explainability Analysis of AI Text Detectors Under Domain Shift
entry.summary: Specificity Bias and the Wikipedia Paradox: An xAI Analysis of AI Text Detectors under Domain Shift arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines how well Transformer-based AI text detectors (DistilBERT, RoBERTa) hold up under domain shift and how they make decisions. The authors test them on a custom dataset of hyper-local news generated by open-source LLMs and analyze them with SHAP-based explainable AI. They report several biases and argue that purely statistical detection methods have systematic limits in highly structured human writing.

entry.title: Proper scoring rules that respect graph structure for finding a single node
entry.summary: Strictly proper scoring rules for node selection tasks on graphs arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies node selection, where the goal is to identify one unknown target node in a graph and the estimator outputs a probability distribution over nodes. The authors introduce two strictly proper, graph-aware scoring rules: the parameter-free Resistance score and the Diffusion score with adjustable coarse-graining resolution. Experiments on epidemic source detection and ImageNet classification show that these scores detect estimation-quality differences that classical metrics miss.

entry.title: A human-verified AI workflow for labeling environmental sound recordings
entry.summary: A Human-Verified AI Workflow for Annotating Environmental Sound Data arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper describes a human-AI workflow used to annotate the Kenya Forest Sounds Dataset (KFSD), a working collection of 7,531 recordings across 21 categories. The fine-tuned Audio Spectrogram Transformer reached 89.36% accuracy for binary detection of person talking, below the predefined 95% threshold for autonomous labeling, so its predictions were used as suggestions and checked by a human. The verifier reviewed all 2,337 machine-labeled files and found no false positives, taking about 4.2 seconds per file versus 35 seconds for manual annotation. The hybrid workflow saved about 20.0 hours, or 41%, on the remaining queue.

entry.title: DeepWaveRL: Reinforcement Learning for Seismic Subsurface Velocity Estimation
entry.summary: DeepWaveRL: Self-Supervised Full Waveform Inversion via Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes DeepWaveRL, a framework that applies reinforcement learning to Full Waveform Inversion (FWI), a geophysics method for estimating subsurface velocity from seismic measurements. The authors recast FWI as policy learning, where a policy network predicts velocity maps as actions and a forward operator is used only for simulation. Learning relies on a single global scalar reward based on data misfit, so no gradients from the forward operator are needed. Experiments show competitive performance against supervised and self-supervised baselines.
